content:
THE ENGINE
OF THE CHRISTIAN MINISTRY
(2 Corinthians 5:14)
Devotional sermon preached at Congress
of Evangelical Communications of Huampani
(Peru), Sunday, September 17, 1967.
We have been here exhorting each other, edifying each other, receiving teachings through presentations,
courses and colloquiums. I would say that we have been
polishing and oiling the machinery of our evangelical witness. But what is the engine that
has set in motion and drives all these gears that send the spoken word through the air in
the lilting language of Cervantes, and multiplies the
word written so that the message of salvation
enter through the eyes of children, and speak to the hearts of young people and adults? What is it that keeps
in action to all this instrument of preachers,
broadcasters, Sunday school instructors, book sellers and visitors? Some will be quick to say: Prayer; others: the Holy Spirit. I
141
I would call the Holy Spirit the energy that descends
of the Triune God, and to prayer the contact of it;
but what, in reality, is the driving force behind such
activity?
I believe that the passage read from 2nd Corinthians gives us
the answer. There we find a man who is
a marvel of packaging activity. It could be
a rabbi comfortably situated in Jerusalem, occupying a chair in his teacher's college
Gamaliel; or a Roman patrician in his comfortable
home of Tarsus of Cilicia; but he is tireless
globetrotter, running from nation to nation and from
continent to continent along the shores of the Mediterranean. A spontaneous preacher insulted in the
synagogues, persecuted in the cities, stoned,
put in jail, booed for hours on end,
who announces the Gospel by day and works by night;
He writes long letters, receives visitors and attends with
I request the consultations of numerous churches.
His activity is so extraordinary and his dedication so passionate, that some go so far as to say that
he is crazy (v. 13). The apostle defends his wisdom and his
prudence alluding to the hope of another life;
(vv. 1, 9 and 10); and ends up taking an exam
impartial before the conscience of his detractors (v. 11).
After this, opening the doors wide
of his soul, he declares to everyone the secret of his amazing life. Following the previous metaphor, I would say that
takes us into the engine room of your own being
moral, and shows us at the center of its amazing
142
personality a powerful dynamo, connected with
all the activities of his apostolic life: "Behold
–he exclaims– the secret of what surprises and admires you.
Behold the power that moves life, hands,
feet of this man incomprehensible to you;
of this apparent madman. It is:
1) The secret of love (vv. 14, 15).
It's about crazy in love. Earned, and closely united to Him who with his life, his death, and his imponderable sacrifice, conquered your heart and ignited it in this living flame, moves to the
impulse of this sublime power. «The love of Christ
“it constrains me”; drives me, throws me, pushes me
to all the activities you admire; well, like
says in another place, "Woe to me if I do not announce the
Gospel…!”
Is this our case, brothers? Let's examine
this morning our hearts before God. what is
the true impulse that moves our activities and our companies for the communication of the
Gospel?
Is it the money? Are we mere professionals of the
work of God?
Is it pride? May our
work and our initiatives by our own and strangers?
(See the anecdote The Dream of a Shepherd.) What would be
the result of an analysis of our zeal? for what
do we live?
143
Who do we live for? Is the love of Christ the
sole and true driving force of our
lives?
It has been said that Christianity is a spiritual idyll... This is how John declares it: "We love Him."
Him because He loved us first."  Our conversion and
our consecration to your service, are but a
logical, natural response to the love that we were
object.Several times I have preached on the topic "Love
"who tied Christ to the cross" and I have illustrated it with the
anecdote The martyr and the chains (see).
How do we respond? Is it true that we serve Christ out of love; with a love
as pure, as loyal, as true as the one He had
for us?
2) Love must be reciprocated.
As a child, I used to visit a Physics teaching laboratory, located at the top of Tibidabo,
where, among many other curious experiments,
we were shown that of the sound correspondence.
A string tuned to a certain pitch, when struck,
produced a sound wave that vibrated,
and even in motion, another string tuned to the same pitch located a few meters away. For
It was a wonder for us to see how the sympathetic chord responded with the same tone to the vibration of
its homogeneous, without anyone touching it. here is one
144
illustration of how the love of Christ finds echo in
hearts tuned by the Holy Spirit.
Have you not noticed how this seems to be the great
concern of Christ, in the famous passage of
Matthew 16? When Jesus first announces his
redemptive death to his disciples, after rebuking Peter who tried to lead him astray
of the sacrifice, he immediately exclaims: "If anyone
If you want to come after me, deny yourself...
because whoever wants to save his life will lose it..."
Joining this verse to 26: «What will it profit
man if he gains the whole world and loses his
soul?"
We have applied this passage many times to the
unconverted But verse 26 is for the unsaved, and verse 27 is for us. We know that the
Salvation is not by works, but the reward is.
It could be the case of saving the soul and losing the
life, that is, the great opportunity that represents
our life in God's plan, for not having known
or wanted to dedicate it to the only thing that has an impact
and reward in eternity. (See the Naive anecdote
children's prayer.)
Will the Lord find in us works of love, of
legitimate affection and gratitude that allow you the satisfaction of placing a large credit on our account?
Will we make our brief and despicable life a
resounding success for eternity?
145
3) Love must be tenacious.
This is the condition of true love. Have you
seen what two who really love each other do
when they collide with the opposition of parents, relatives
or friends? How many dramas of human love do they have?
in tension the hearts of thousands of readers of
novels or spectators of the big and small
screen! However, many who are excited
For some fictitious love they have heard of a love
sublime, not of a human being, but divine, who
He sacrificed for them without having any need to
love them, nor suffer to such an extent and, nevertheless,
remain indifferent, or are easily intimidated
in the face of opposition or persecution to which love
Christ would expose them (Matthew 13:21). Thank God,
However, his love has found an echo in some
hearts here and beyond the ocean in people who
can declare like Peter: "Lord, you know all
the things; "You know we love you."
4) Love is ingenious.
These days I have enjoyed visiting the Congress exhibition, examining, in addition to interesting books, ingenious audiovisual methods that
in it they are exhibited. What made my heart happy was
to think that the brains and hands that had
devised all those curious systems of presenting the message of Christ to children and adults, which
They had done more than money for the fiery
desire that they feel to make clear and accessible the
146
message of Christ. Love is always ingenious and
Sometimes difficulty sharpens ingenuity and initiative.
(See the anecdote Ingenious resources in times of
intolerance.)
Some foreign brothers have shown
admiration for such incidents, but I do not see inThis is nothing extraordinary. I am sure that many sincere Christians, in the countries you represent, would do exactly the same, or perhaps much the same.
more, of having found themselves in the same circumstances that we found ourselves in those times, because they also love Christ.
5) Love is permanent.
“It never ceases to be” – affirms the apostle Paul.
Is it like that in us? How many times does it seem better
flashing! Easily turns on and off
like sparkler or chip fire! They have passed
few years since the time of our difficulties
in Spain, and sometimes we are tempted to say
that we would need another era of intolerance. We have jealousy and misunderstanding, selfishness and strife, like everywhere. Is it not because it was not
All pure gold that shone in difficult days?
They were, yes, nuggets of gold, of true love for our
Savior; but intertwined with great pride
personal, church, denominational or company.
God has to evaluate our zeal through
tests. How can we make it so that it is only
pure gold our service? Because, brothers, "the
147
"shepherd's dream" must be a reality for each one
of us before x years; maybe much less
than we think. What reasons will you find in our service then? Let us leave this assembly with the sincere purpose of putting more fire in
our life; more power in action.
Let us remember the cross. The divine force that Christ
manifested when “he strengthened his countenance to go to Jerusalem”; the courage and tenacity he showed when walking
from Gethsemane to the Praetorium, to carry the cross and to
stay in it despite all the incitements
to decline his saving company... We, saved by his grace and his servants, let us ask for the
same strength, same power, same decision
to correspond with dignity in our service.
ANECDOTES
A SHEPHERD'S DREAM
It is said of a certain pastor that after a tiring and triumphant Sunday in which he had delivered a
eloquent sermon that aroused enthusiasm, congratulations and decisions, he sat, tired, in the large armchair of the
pulpit and falling asleep he had the following dream:
He saw the majestic figure of the Savior enter through the door of the temple and advance along the central aisle towards
him. The shepherd fell to his knees and through that phenomenon
psychic that allows us to reason during sleep without
realize the impossibility of what we are
148
Dreaming, he exclaimed: Do you honor me up to this point, Lord? How much
You consider me, that you deign to visit me! But the majestic
The figure of the Savior simply says: "How is your zeal?"
The preacher feels his zeal as something tangible within
from his chest, he takes it out and hands it to his august visitor.
He puts it on a scale and the shepherd hears with satisfaction.
say: "100 pounds." Then he sees that with blows of a hammer the stone breaks like weak sand and the Lord goes
separating the different particles of precious metal from
other conglomerates. The pastor watches with anxious anxiety as he writes the result. Finally extends the
hand to collect the expected analysis and read the following:
Pride of denomination 20% Wood
Church Pride 35% Hay
Personal Pride 40% Leaf Litter
Love of souls 2% Gold
Love of God 3% Pure
    — —
Total ………………………… 100%
Faced with the shock that produces such a terrible result,
The shepherd wakes up and physically falls to his knees this time,
asking now that when the reality of what comes
has anticipated your subconscious may your balance be
much better.
What would be the result of the analysis of this of ours
zeal for the work that we are carrying out and that
Have we enjoyed exhibiting these days?
149
THE MARTYR AND THE CHAINS
In days of persecution, when a certain martyr was taken away
to the bonfire, he raised a prayer expressing the joy that
felt for the privilege of sealing the testimony of his faith with
his own life.“I thank you, Lord,” said the noble martyr, “because today is the day of my victory; today I will see you and
I will be with you for all ages.
The executioner, moved and attentive to the words of the
noble witness of Christ, left loose the chains that
They tied him to the execution post. Then the martyr,
Lowering his head, he exclaimed:
–However, my friend, hold the chains well.
Why did the noble martyr give such a warning? because
even when the spirit was ready, he knew that the flesh
was weak, and feared that not being able to endure the pain of
fire, the instinct of self-preservation made him jump from the
flames and accomplish, in such an hour of trial, what so many
times he had refused: to apostatize from his faith.
But what chains tied Jesus Christ to the cross?
When the servants of Caiaphas went to arrest him in the
garden of Gethsemane, three times they fell to the ground,
which Christ gave proof of his supernatural power. with
with the same ease he could have freed himself from his enemies in the anguishing moments of Calvary.
“Get off the cross,” his friends told him in a mocking tone.
enemies.
—Come down and save us too, if you are the Son
of God – cried his fellow prisoners.
–Get off the cross –he advised him and even demanded his
human nature in the face of pain that seemed unbearable.
150
However, He did not exercise His omnipotence to deliver Himself. We can, therefore, say that what held Christ
on the cross of Calvary was nothing but the chains of his
deep love for each of the needy sinners.
We can imagine the Savior as hearing, in his
wisdom, the voices of thousands of sinners tell him:
«Suffer for us, blessed Messiah, fulfill the redemption, and we will love you, we will glorify you and we will be faithful
witnesses of your love, in our earthly life and for the
eternal centuries." This love and hope was, without a doubt,
who kept Christ suffering for us on the cross,
until he could exclaim: "It is finished."
NAIVE YOUTH PRAYER
The author remembers that in the days of his youth,
When he was preparing to preach the Gospel,
read the book Jesus is Coming, by James H. Conkey, and received such
impact of the next coming of the Lord, which fell on
his knees and prayed, thanking the Lord for his coming,
adding: "Lord, if possible, delay it for a few years,
so that I may have the opportunity to serve You, and win some souls for You.
INGENIOUS RESOURCES IN TIMES OF INTOLERANCE
In the difficult days of the postwar period in Spain, the
Evangelical believers had to appeal to ingenious
ways to carry out our testimony. The
cults were celebrated in the houses, since almost all
temples were closed. In some towns
151
This was done with a certain tolerance on the part of the
local authorities, but in certain places surveillance was very close and sanctions frequent.
In Medina del Campo (Valladolid), where the police
He frequently hovered around the house where he lived.
They celebrated services, and more than once he had entered
to wait and punish with a fine all those who went
arriving, and with imprisonment for the owners of the house, the believers were warned whether or not there was danger in entering,
using a jug placed on the street balcony (like
It is customary there, and more so in those times, to keep the water fresh). In this way, with a simple look at the balcony, attendees knew if they could enter safely or if they had to pass by that day, and
thus avoiding an encounter with the police. An invitation to
same police officers to drink fresh water, or a drink of water
drunk unnecessarily by some of the inhabitants of the
house, was the excuse to place the pitcher in the position
agreed with other believers.
In the city of Terrassa, after two years of celebrating the
cults around the houses, there were about 16 people who had to
be baptized To this end, we invite all members to come on a certain Sunday to the pastoral house, adjacentto the church. During the week we had removed
beware the government seal affixed to an interior door
that gave access to the temple. The baptistery was cleansed and
prepared. Believers were warned to stand
around the pulpit. After the act has been carried out, and
when we were preparing to put the seal of
closure, we realized that even when the dust
on the pews was intact, the presence of the congregation was revealed by the footsteps on the floor.
windy soil. How to avoid evidence in case of
inspection?
We went to buy a bag of earthy-colored cement
and we began to throw handfuls into the air, until
a cloud of dust became that, settling gently
especially the place, completely covered the footprints, leaving it with the appearance that no one had entered the place.
prohibited area.

content:

They try all their lives without success. There is the

to many who are not really.
Were Caesar, Napoleon,

Even among those who acquire their renown through more honest means (statesmen, writers, singers,

violin, having a good voice, giving a good thrust to a bull or a skillful kick to a ball, not

(See the anecdote Dr. Duff's speech.) Jesus calls
great only to this class of men, who

It is only great in your presence
He who has excellence
To know oneself inferior.

Every day smaller,

(See the anecdote The little boat built and bought.)
This is our case. Not only did the Creator employ thousands
182

made in his image, but, foreseeing that the

Friend, don't you want Him to apply such a glorious price to you? May He buy you, so that you can

blood.)
If you have already accepted Christ as your Savior and

What gives rise to the bitter complaint of Luke 6:46? So

Remember the circumstances of this story. The

183
The order was for them to go back to Jerusalem (Acts 1:4). However, instead, they lingered in Galilee.
To a certain extent it was natural, being in the
region where they had their relatives and friends;
but this led them to the temptation of returning to their old job, dawdling longer than they should. «A
I go fishing”; It wasn't bad at all...; but now they were

24:47 and John 20:21).
That's how it is with us many times. They are not bad

"hobbies", sports, but we must keep in mind that Christians are called to a duty
top: "Serve Christ." "Work, not for food, for it perishes" (John 6:27). What do we do for

3. Jesus comes out to meet
   of those who have lost their vision
It was necessary to make them recognize, that handful of disciples, who had forgotten their lordship,
his orders, his superior occupations..., to Him, in

Lord chased away the fish in that sad and long
184
night. In the same way, our adversities
They prepare for the instruction that He wants to give us.
As the farmer turns the earth before sowing it, Christ sometimes shakes his people with adversities and setbacks to lead us along his path.
way. (See the anecdote Hans Egede, the first
Danish missionary to the Lapps.) Similarly,
In the present case the Lord redirected his disciples to their duty, taking away their fishing. Not in vain
He had told them: "Without Me, you can do nothing."  and this
It is a reality even in the material order for those who
We are children of God. When they were not disciples, the

Today people in the world do whatever they want:

They are not from the Lord. The fisherman Pedro had never spent a night like that in the productive sea
from Galilee. Would you not feel the voice of the Lord on your conscience due to such adversity?
b) He appears in person and they don't know him.  there it is

c) The eye of faith distinguishes the Lord. It was John, the disciple of love, the first to distinguish him, and Peter,
the most determined, the one who jumps into the water. wants

despite his denial. It doesn't say: what do I care?
me?

God by the Holy Spirit, but you do. You have enjoyed

If you belong to Christ… if He is your Kurios? It is not possible

It is not enough to have Him in such a concept for great things, forgetting that He is in everything, and that He is
Omniscient and Omnipresent. Only then will you feel joyful.
We all have Christ as Lord in a general and distant sense; but not with that attitude that
David expresses in Psalm 123:2. Those servants
Hebrews did not wait for the verbal order, they tried to
divine it in the eyes of their lords in order to demonstrate their deep attention and obedience. Is it from this
how we maintain communion
with God?
186
But alas, this attitude of David was not constant in his life! He looked into the eyes of his Lord many times
times when he was in conflict, or in a
spiritual euphoria, like when he brought the ark to Jerusalem; but not the day he climbed up onto the roof lazily
to look around the neighbors' houses and saw
Bethsheba. That's how it is sometimes in the lives of
Christians. It is easy to see the Lord in worship and hear
your voice in the reading of your Word or in some book
pious, but the secret of the Christian life is to live
in the presence of the Lord. This attitude of believers
unconsecrated has two bad results:
1) Enjoy little spiritual communion, which
causes the deepest joy in the Christian soul,
greater than all worldly joys.
2) Reach the end of life, to the beaches of
eternity, as the disciples arrived on this occasion, with the boat empty.
4. The lordship resumed
Even though the disciples were far away at sea, the
Lord was waiting for you. His presence attracted them

«Paidos, he says to them, do you have anything to eat?» The ancient translators of our Bible used the expression that they judged most appropriate so as not to cause
strangeness to the readers of the N.T., putting the word
187
«boys»; but the revised one more appropriately translates “little children,” although, literally, it is “children.” Affectionate word, but also reproachful. Weren't they acting like children? Instead of dealing with
the high mission of “sent ones” to forgive sins
(John 20:22, 23) –or to cause sins to be forgiven–, so that immortal souls could find the secret of eternal life, as happened in
Pentecost… having fun catching fish!
How many times must we Christians seem
children to the angels when we occupy ourselves with excessive and inappropriate interest in what has no value! The
apostle exhorts us: «Be children in malice, but
men in the sense.
But many times we are completely the opposite:
"Men in malice and children in meaning."
And worse still, poorly raised children; obedient
only when you follow your taste. This is how many of us act
times the current disciples of the Lord.
How many say that they cannot go to the temple because they are tired; but on Monday they go to the factory
tired or not. They recognize a lordship in the personwho gives them material bread, who do not recognize the
Sir. How many times do we abuse Him, recognizing Him as Savior, as friend, theoretically as
God, but not as "Lord"!
a) Discovery followed by action. When
The eye of love discovers the Lord, the action follows.
Pedro throws himself into the sea, the others approach, they obey
like a stranger, automatically. But in
188
Peter and John had a higher meaning. John, speaking to his companion of the Lord, Peter, launching himself
to meet him. This is how faith and love work, with
acts. If you love Him, you will talk about Him to your neighbor,
you will mention instinctively; you will go to the temple,
You will do the things that please Him. you don't want
keep you separate from their communion.
b) The tragedy of coldness. But the others
disciples are stunned, inhibited;
"without daring to ask him, knowing that it was the Lord."
What an accurate picture of the situation of many
Christians! Deep down, we love him, we recognize him;
Maybe we would do something great if persecution came or someone provoked us by insulting Christ;
because we love him..., but we feel ashamed of
open your mouth for Him under normal circumstances; we are too lazy to pray.
The author of this appendix to the Gospel of John,
points out this detail, which someone would tell him, with
strangeness: "No one dared..." Did the fact of seeing him resurrected overwhelm you with fear? It is possible, but in
other times it was not like that. When he took them to the mountain
of the ascension, they asked him questions; the women
They threw them at his feet the day they saw him resurrected.
Why not now…? Because he had caught them in
fraganti, fishing, when they should have been in Jerusalem

mute, the intimate communion broken; without being able to speak
Lord as a friend. In Mark 6:30 we are told
that the apostles met with Jesus and told him
189
everything they had done; but then they had something
to tell him, now there was nothing. This is why they were
mute, obeying, bringing the net eating,
but without intimacy, frankness, or freedom.
5. The confirmed lordship
Jesus breaks the silence with the three questions
Pedro, guilty of that scene, since it was he who suggested going fishing. "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?"
Surely I had already told him that the first afternoon
of his resurrection (Luke 24:34) and he had demonstrated it with his impulsive attitude right now; but for
three times he wants to hear it from his mouth before his companions; and before them ratify him in his ministry
apostolic, with a phrase that is at the same time a
rebuke: "Feed my sheep." What it implies:
«This is not your place, fulfill your ministry; not of
to catch fish, but to catch men for my kingdom.
Jesus had said it a few weeks ago in the Upper Room: "If you love me, keep my commandments."
What is our attitude? That of poorly raised, disobedient and stubborn children, or that of faithful servants,
grateful to his precious redemption and friends of the
Sir? (See the Domini Sumas anecdote.)
May He help us to always feel, as without a doubt
We feel in these moments that He is truly
our Lord and who deserves our most selfless and
faithful service.
190
ANECDOTES
THE BOAT BUILT AND BOUGHT
A very crafty child built with great patience
and he made a beautiful little boat with its sail, rudder and rigging, so that it looked like a real boat. but
one day, trying to make him navigate the river, the current
took it and put it out of reach, without being able to
recover it. With great sadness he returned home, no
being able to get the lost toy out of your mind.
A couple of weeks later, as I passed by
an establishment of lance objects, saw his
ship. Yes, indeed, it was his. I knew him in so many details…! He went in to claim it, but the owner of the
establishment did not listen to reason. He told him it would be
yours if you bought it, and nothing more. The boy went to his
home, opened the piggy bank and paid the price for what had beenhis. When I carried him, caressing his little treasure,
said:
–Little boat, now I love you more, because you are mine two
times. Firstly because I built you and then because
I bought you.
THE SLAVE RESCUED WITH BLOOD
A black slave ran desperately through the
jungle of Africa in the direction of a certain Mission House in search
of refuge. He had angered his irate master, who
He had sworn to kill him, and ran after him with his bow drawn,
hoping to have him within range to stick the arrow in his
entrails
191
The director came out at the door of the Mission and seeing the
dangerous scene began to shout to the pursuer,
begging him to refrain from shooting; but the man,
Ignoring him, he continued running after his victim without giving him any respite. At the moment when the fugitive
He was about to throw himself at the missionary's feet begging for protection, the pursuer fired his bow. Quickly the
missionary extended his arm and received the arrow that
It was going to stick into the neck of the pursued. of the arm
blood began to flow, which splashed on the poor black man
kneeling at his feet.
“You have shed English blood,” exclaimed the missionary, addressing the aggressor severely. why not
Did you listen when he yelled at you to stop? do you know
what can this cost you? –in those times the
The British flag was highly respected by its subjects.
of its vast colonial empire. Only on one condition
–the missionary continued– I will not report to the authorities
of what you have done: That you give me your slave, refusing to kill him.
The slave, who in addition to saving his life recovered his
freedom, he did not know how to evaluate the generous action of the
missionary. Every time he told the story he felt not
not only favored, but highly honored to be able to say:
"He bought me with his blood."
HANS EGEDE,
FIRST DANISH MISSIONARY TO THE LAPPANS
When God called the first missionary Hans Egede
to Greenland, this was a highly esteemed Danish shepherd
of his congregation.
192
He communicated to his wife the desire that God had placed
in his heart to bring the knowledge of the Gospel to
the inhabitants of the frozen North; but she opposed him
tenaciously. Should they leave their comfortable home and
beloved congregation, which they had pastored for many
years, to go live among inhabitants of ice houses,
pagans, superstitious and backward, sharing their
miserable life?
In vain, Hans Egede showed his companion the
order of Christ: "Go into all the world."
-Yeah! But why us precisely? -argued the
wife–. Have there not been Lapps for centuries in the
frozen northern shores? Why is no Christian
Had such an idea occurred to you until then?
But there came a day when God disturbed the comfortable nest of the Egede couple, and they began to emerge.
thorns Complaints arose in the Danish congregation; Both sides wanted the pastor to give them the
reason. Every day news of complaints and murmurings against the pastor arrived. Then the wife was
first to recognize and confess:
–Why would something so sad have happened in our
church, Hans? Could it be that God calls us to work
missionary in Greenland and we are outside the
path of your will?
In this way began the Christian work that transformed and brought the joy and hope of Christ to the sad
inhabitants of the North Pole. And joy also in the heart
of the Egede shepherds, seeing that it had not been in vain
his obedience to God's call.
193
«DOMINI SUMUS»
Martin Luther traveled on foot often. In certain
occasion he asked for accommodation in a peasant house that
They treated him as well as they could.
Knowing that he was the famous reformer, they refused
all payment, but they asked him to remember them in
his prayers and wrote in red ink on his
some souvenir inscription on the wall.
Luther wrote “Domini sumus”. The peasant
asked what those words meant, and Luther
He explained that in correct Latin they can have a double meaning, depending on the context of the phrase."They mean," he said, "we are the Lord's," but they can
also mean "We are gentlemen", which is precisely
the opposite, applying them in the opposite direction.
But Luther gave them a useful spiritual lesson
combining both senses:
“We belong to the Lord,” he told them, “because He bought us.”
with his blood but this same thing makes us free
by his grace, and let us no longer be slaves of Satan, nor
of any man, but gentlemen, truly free
to no longer serve sin and to voluntarily honor and glorify Him.
Good motto! Let's write it on the walls of our
heart.

content:
(Hebrews 3:12-14)
Introduction
We are in vacation time. Many of you have
spent a few days of solace, away from work
daily routine enjoying the greenery, charm
and magnificence of the heights, or of the caresses of the
sea And you will have to start (or you have started)
In x days the daily work, with its fatigue, its
worries, their difficulties and disappointments.
This is why I think it is appropriate to talk to you about work.
and rest from the human point of view and
spiritual.
1. Work and divine rest
Work is a universal law. God himself works in
its high sphere, and also rests, or we would say, increases and decreases its creative and organizing activity
in certain places in the Universe.
What does it mean if not Genesis 2:1-3? For this,
when I hear people say that this world has so many cen195
thenars of millions of years, or that the rock or the fossil
found in this or that place in the earth's crust
must have too, I'm not saying no; but I stay
somewhat doubtful.
Do you know why? Because it seems to me that scientists judge things by the current rhythm of nature, according only to their current experience. That is, they judge and calculate based on what
They know, but what about what they don't know? We know today, for
For example, what was unknown thirty years ago, that
by means of isotopic radiation they can be made
apparent miracles. What plants exposed to suitable conditions to radioactivity can grow?
in days and become gigantic. Perhaps this explains the
existence of the imposing antediluvian animals
that preceded the creation of man! maybe
one day science will have to recognize, not only what it is already forced to admit now, that
There were six different epochs, days of creation, and their
ordered succession, in the exact way it describes
the Bible, but also that in those six epochs
creatively things got done faster. In others
words: that God worked with extraordinary activity during those aforementioned six epochs
geological, and rested – or rather, is resting
still – in the seventh, the current one; in which the matter
is slowly losing radioactivity, without receiving
new creative and organizing power.
Perhaps this explains the fact
strange, given the countless resources of the Natu196
nature, as we see them manifested in this
world, that we are surrounded by worlds
companions of the earth in the same planetary system of the Sun, so backward, next to which we
we inhabit Then perhaps it will be recognized that if
our planet is so different from the moon and others
planets of the same geological age, it is not only because
the physical causes to which they attribute such
difference, so we find exposed in
Genesis 1:2, that is, God worked with an activity
extraordinary, and especially intentional about
the earth during the six epochs of creation, and
Now we are in the seventh, when the Creator
rests, that is, it does not intervene except very rarely in
the physical aspect, in this wonderful world where
we live, while it has not seen fit to intervene
in a particular way on these planets.
2. Human work and rest
When the great invisible Artificer ceased to act
directly on the physical elements, that is, he rested, gave to man, created in his image and likeness,
the labor law, so that it completed its magnificent
works taking advantage of the wonderful order by Him
established, and of the natural resources provided by
his wise providence on our planet.
a) Work is not a punishment. He didn't give him the job
as a punishment, but as a privilege; the privilege
to cooperate with his heavenly Father in perfecting
ment of this world He put this object in a
kind of museum or botanical garden prepared in the
Asia Minor, the paradise of Eden. Note that
There was gold, the most manageable metal, precious stones, water sources, trees, plants and animals.
of all kinds (Genesis 2:10-15). «Here is everything,at least the original types that have later been
developed in races – it seems to tell him –; use it. nothing
It will be contrary to you, but everything favorable; works, not in
the terms of a task, but of a distraction and
satisfaction." Without thistles or thorns, without pests with
to fight, the first human farmer had no
a heavy task, much less it would have been
have been able to use the instruments that scientific knowledge (more quickly achieved
had the tragedy of sin not occurred) they would have
provided shortly after. The work that God
given to Adam was nothing more than a privilege of collaboration;
like the father who allows the child to put his little hand
on the handle of the basket, to make it look like it's doing
something... «So that you can choose the plants and fruits
that you feel like it –God seems to tell him–; put the seed and cover it with soil. This is all. Of the rest I
I'm in charge, because you, poor creature, can do nothing more."
b) 
Sin, curse of work.  But it came
sin, the criminal virus of distrust of God,
with its sequel of malevolent feelings; ambition, selfishness, envy, hatred. The simple act
of taking and taking from the forbidden tree was just the
198
first manifestation, the first fruit of the terrible
seed of evil, of contagion, of the plague of sin
that emerged from hell in the person of the Tempter.
Then work appeared as punishment, as
drudgery, like a fight with hostile forces
of Nature; and even worse than everything, with strength
hostile within humanity itself. If the sin
It would have been a mere act and not an infection; a
wrong act that he had to receive as punishment
the expulsion from Eden would not have been anything serious. A
day or another the men had to spread out over
the earth, leaving the «Didactic Museum School of
God", to colonize the world. But it wasn't this
only, but sin corrupted the heart of the
man, making him capable of criminal acts; him
transformed from a son of God into a criminal in
power. When they saw the men killing
from his neighbors he obtained the advantage of seizing
of their property and their women, using the extraordinary intelligence with which God had endowed them,
They began to shape the stones and forge the
metals, not only to defend themselves against beasts, but
to war with each other. From Lamech, the great-grandson of Cain,
We read that when someone offended him and hit him, he
He murdered him at random, and warned his two wives
Ada and Zilla: "Whoever touches me, I liquidate" (Genesis
4:23, 24). But, as the saying goes, "where
they give them they take", other men did the same, and
The earth began to be filled with violence until it reached
to the depravity that the flood brought.
199
For this reason, before and after the flood, men dedicated themselves to forming groups, naming a leader, to better protect themselves from their enemies;
They built walled cities; wars arose
between tribes and between groups of tribes; were made
prisoners and the human tragedy of the
slavery, which has lasted for centuries, and has made painful
and miserable the lives of millions of human beings,
instead of fulfilling the ideal plan of the Creator, of
family independence, mostly agricultural, in a
abundant world for all and well distributed. In
Hebrews 2:15 describes to us the sad condition of
the fallen race by saying: "For fear of death
"They were subject to servitude all their lives." In
Indeed, in past centuries, because of wars and
a social organization marred by sin,
millions of men worked from dawn to dusk, nothing
more than for a miserable pittance that would allow them to continue living. The millions of slaves who
They built the pyramids of Egypt, the walls of
Tarragona, the great wall of China, etc., etc., not
They had another rest, day after day and year after year, more
than the brief hours of the night. It did not exist for
them nor the weekly rest, exclusive of the nation
Hebrew by God's command, nor times ofvacation like the ones we have today. How grateful we should be to live, today, in a society that, although far from being perfect, is,
unfailingly, better than that of those dark
times.
200
c) Work in the Kingdom of God.  Because He is
who holds the future of the world in his hand, the
picture that the prophecies of the kingdom of God give us
on earth is different from the one he presented to us
certain television program, talking about the
housing and pollution problems in
the year 2000. Because we believe that the Lord must
intervene before humanity reaches the
state that human thinkers envision, we know that in that happy time of the future,
"Everyone will sit under his vine and under his
fig tree” (Micah 4:4). This means that humanity, under divine rule, will return to earth,
distributed equitably, and will enjoy the benefits of a civilization extraordinarily developed by contact with heaven... They will live the
men spread around the world, not concentrated
in large capitals, totally redeemed from
hard work by machines that only
They will have to speak so that their electromagnetic computers will take them to do all kinds of arduous tasks.
3. An eternal vocation
But the perspective of the future is still very much
more flattering for the redeemed of God; those who
During this time of trial they put their trust
in Christ and lived facing the future: «There remains one
rest for the people of God", we read in the letter
201
to the Hebrews. Practically, and in the light of prophetic teachings, there remains an eternal vacation.
Indeed, what do we do during the holidays?
Abandoning heavy work, we try
change the environment, we go to other places
to enjoy more and better the good things that
God has put in this world. And this is what we
awaits in the Kingdom of Heaven.
a) Security of the heavenly vacation. The Jews
They had little knowledge of the afterlife. For the
Most of them God's blessings were coded
in the present. For this reason, the apostle tries to show them that the rest promised by God to parents
It was not just the earthly Canaan, as some thought. King David had already entered and lived in
Canaan when he exhorts fidelity to God in order
not to lose the promised rest. If Joshua had given them rest – the text says – he would not speak after another day.
This rest exists and is not death, as some think. Death, as the end of existence, is not
It is rest. Skeletons cannot be said to rest, because rest is the opposite of tiredness, and
what is not tired cannot rest. Implies
the enjoyment of rest. The farmer rests lying on the grass, the horse rests in the manger, or in the meadow, but the horse does not literally rest.
cart or hoe, because they are inert instruments
that they neither get tired nor can they rest. The rest
202
It does not mean, therefore, to cease to exist, or to cease to be, but rather
enjoy a better existence, free of work
painful, and this is exactly heaven: not a state
of inactivity, but of delightful and glorious service
(Revelation 22:4 and Ephesians 3:10). (See, as an extension of this idea, the books When He Comes, pp.
220 and 221; Nothing or the Stars, pp. 313-324; and he
Heaven, pp. 189 to 209.)
b) Working for true rest.  We have said that God acts in two spheres, the physical and the spiritual. When his activity in the physical sphere ceased,
began the great moral and spiritual work of repairing
the disastrous work of Satan and "redeem for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works." Jesus considered himself a worker for God in this area, and he says "My
Father works until now, and I work” (John 5:17).
"It is expedient for me to do the works of him who sent me"
(John 9:4).
«I have glorified you on earth, I have finished the
work that you gave me to do, now glorify me
about Yourself” (John 17:4, 5).Here is the same law of work and rest,
even in this very elevated sphere, that of the Son of God
working for a lost world. us
We are the beneficiaries of the redemptive work of
Christ. But for what?
c) Our work for the Kingdom. Ephesians 2 us
exposes the divine plan in a very clear way: To the
that "we were dead he gave us life." "We are saved by grace," but "that we may walk in the
203
good works prepared by God. Not a dead man
can work. Those who are dead in crimes and
sins can do many good works according to
the world, but they cannot take part in the work
most importantly, to communicate the good news of
salvation to lost souls, since they themselves do not
They understand nothing in this area; but the simplest
believer can do it, especially among those of his
sphere. A risen with Christ has been saved for
serve, to live an effective and active Christian life.
This is why Jesus said it (John 6:27). The worst is when
The cares of this life prevent us from fulfilling the
Christian duties. When we are cold spiritually, we do not feel like glorifying God; nor with
our time or with our money.
Our text presents the case of the Israelites
who left Egypt and walked in the desert;
but they did not reach Canaan because their hearts
filled with disbelief, they felt tired of following the cloud... This same thing has happened to some,
in the spiritual realm. We have seen them active and
jealous, but only for a time. They got tired,
not in the service of God, but of serving God. but
if we have been faithful, if we have lived for Christ, if
We have glorified him on earth as Christ glorified the Father, our works will follow us (Revelation 14:13). Maybe nothing remains here, or is erased in
few years, but it will remain there. For this we can
to say that it is beautiful to get tired serving God...
Such are promised happy and true rest204

content:
(Jeremiah 29:11;
Romans 8:28-32)
Introduction
One of the proofs of the origin and higher purpose of
man is that he is a being capable of anticipating the future..., he has ideals and aspirations. The animals are
what modern philosophy calls existential: they
They do live only and exclusively in the present moment, they do not worry about the future nor do they have the capacity to anticipate the future; but the man
think of what was and what will be, and direct your
efforts in accordance with their forecasts. The little bird
He does not worry about whether there will be no food tomorrow;
He fills his crop and begins to sing satisfied. But he
man worries and directs his cares towards tomorrow
with excess, without giving room to God.
It is not bad to be foresight, but it is bad to strive for
the future as if everything depended on us. Of
there is Christ's warning in Matthew 6:25-34. Someone said: "What has made me suffer the most in
"Life is what has never happened." This is for lack
206
of trust in God. We don't feel as we should that Someone above thinks of us.
However, God himself assures us in
many passages of Holy Scripture, and with
many examples from history.
One of the most specific cases is this one, related to the people of Israel during the exile.
Babylonian.
1. The historical motif of the divine promise
We know that after the taking of Jerusalem
By the Assyrians, the best of the Hebrew people were taken captive to Babylon. The longing was very vivid
among the people far from their homeland, as we
demonstrates Psalm 137. It seems likely that, with
reason for the madness of King Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel
4) and the consequent misgovernment that would result,
The idea of fleeing and returning to Jerusalem spread among the exiles. King Joachin had rebelled, perhaps taking advantage of the same situation. Let's go
help the patriotic monarch, the emigrants would say
forces of Babylon. It was a risky undertaking and
recklessness that, logically, had to end in
disaster, given the distance and scarce resources of
a people recently subjected to slavery; but three
false prophets, Ahab and Zedekiah (who should not be
confuse with the kings of that name who lived
above), as well as a false prophet called
Shemaiah encouraged them to flee. For this reason, the
207
God's true prophet, Jeremiah, sent them from
Jerusalem a secret letter, which had nothing of
pessimistic, but realistic, advising them not to
move from Babylon. He warns them that two of the
false prophets would die executed by the government
Assyrian, and Shemaiah would save his life by flight, but
He would sadly die in exile, without succession. At
At the same time he gives them the promise from God
that, seventy years after the date of the exile, the Israelite people would return to their homeland.
This was circumstantially fulfilled in the days
of Ezra and Nehemiah, and in a much more
extensive and complete after 2,500 years, in the present time. Note the curious expression: «Of
all the people and all the places where you
I threw,” in verse 14; and the phrase: «I will gather them together
the ends of the earth" in 31:8-10; since the spread at that time did not go to all places
of the earth, but only to Babylon. So the
Jeremiah's prophecy is having its last and most
exact fulfillment, precisely in our own days.
In this verse we find three great and
significant statements that deserve careful consideration:
1. God thinks of us: "I know the thoughts I have about you."
2. God's thoughts differ from appearances: "Thoughts of peace and not evil."
208
3. They coincide with our best aspirations:
"To give you the end you expect."
2. God thinks of us
Is it possible? –some exclaim. what are we
us for Him? An industrialist told me: Are we not to the Creator as ants are?for us? There are so many millions of human beings…! If only God had to think of everyone!… But
The Bible tells us that he does think. We don't
we think of Him as we should, but He thinks
because it is infinite and omniscient. «Your Father
“knows”… –affirms our Lord Jesus Christ.
a) God knows us personally. Not only does he remember, but he has plans about all of us.
We think about our friends, but we have plans for our children. What happy security!
We are not orphans of destiny. Seeing how they go
generations succeeding each other on the earth,
Men wonder: Are we alone and orphaned?
in the infinite universe? Let's see if we have brothers
on some near or far planet…!
2,000 years ago, Someone who proved to be more than
a man, spoke with great confidence of a Father
heavenly and taught us to pray: "Our Father who is
in Heaven..." And this Father has personal plans
about us. The potentates of the earth have general plans, but they cannot have personal plans for each of their subjects. However,
209
In the parable of the good shepherd there is a magnificent phrase: "He calls his sheep by their names," "He knows
the Lord those who are his" (John 10:3 and 14 and 2nd
Timothy 2:19).
b) God's plans are beneficial. «Of peace and not
of evil." There was a doubt in the hearts of the exiled. Is it God's purpose to leave us to
always in exile? He did not deliver us, when we prayed that Nebuchadnezzar might not enter
Jerusalem; that it happened to him like Rabshakeh, and everything happened the other way around. Is it against us? Don't you
will you forgive us?
c) God's plans are slow. So it seems to
our impatience. We build machines that do things faster and faster. We put a mold, and plastic, and a flower comes out after three
seconds. But God's flowers take months to
develop; however, how much more perfect!
So it is with the works of his Providence: they develop
slowly in our opinion.
3. God's plans
    they have no resemblance to appearances
The molds of our machines have a
similar to the result we propose; but
From a small, round seed of God, a
oak. The mold is imperceptible; however; there
It is fixed, in its cells invisible to the naked eye,
the divine purpose as to being, vegetable or animal
bad. The works of God cannot be guessed by their
appearance.
We have all heard of geological ages. Hundreds of thousands of years ago this world
It had exuberant vegetation, but tremendous convulsions of the earth's crust buried those gigantic trees, and when life reappeared,
it was with more appropriate vegetation and fauna
being intelligent, "crown of creation", which God
had been proposed to be placed on the earth.
What does the Creator do?, people might ask.
angelic beings. Why does it destroy so quickly
what has taken centuries to form? but god
was storing in the bowels of the earth the
reserves of coal, oil, and natural gas, which
so useful have they been for man, created at his
image. Thus, in the moral field, God brings good out of
bad. He makes all things work together for good.
Lazarus dies, to the despair of his sisters
who were waiting for the presence of Christ and the miracle.
But how much good came from his death! The most text
comforting and illuminating for all mortals
we have in this beautiful story (John 11:25).
"All these things are against me!" he exclaimed
Jacob.
"Wait a few months, Jacob, and you will see everything turn into good," he could be answered.
Where will we get bread for these to eat?, say the disciples in a hurry. But Jesus knew
what I had to do.
211
God always knows what to do. Such is
the experience of our lives, looking back,
and it will be more fully so when we look at them from
eternity.
4. God's thoughts
    match our best aspirationsOur text has a key word: The end.
“No one is happy until the end,” says the adage. and it is
very true. But the end is not here. Which
are the final aspirations of the human being? Which
are they ours?
1. Knowledge.
The wise man dies aware that he does not know a
tiny part of what I could and would like to know. It
others will be discovered tomorrow, but this does not satisfy the
individual. We would like to know him ourselves… Power
to be part of this humanity of the future that we foresee more advanced than ours. Implicit with the promise of immortality is the promise of knowledge. What a privilege! Now I know in part –he said
Pablo–, but then I will know as I am known.
This is not a mere assumption of the rabbi-philosopher
Saul, but it corresponds to a promise made
for Christ. "I have made known to them Your name and
I will still make it known” (John 17:26). "We will know and continue to know the Lord," he exclaims
the prophet (Hosea 6:3). Our desires to meet
ment of God, of the secrets of his universe, of
his providence and his grace must be satisfied
in eternity.
2. Happiness.
We always go after this ideal. always
excited that we will achieve it a little more
forward. As the poet says:
And the waiting man lives,
And the waiting man dies;
You never get what you expect
And he has what he is hating.
But the psalmist declares: "I will see your
face; I will be satisfied when I wake up to Your likeness” (Psalm 17:15). This means: I will have my aspirations fulfilled when I can contemplate you in the
upper world. Here we only partially see our aspirations fulfilled. I would say that we should not
be as pessimistic as Espronceda; we don't have
always what we are hating. There are good things
also in this life, by the mercy of God;
but not to perfection, and always with bitterness
to see that they are transitory, when our being aspires to the eternal.
3. The glory of God.
Do you have this aspiration? Do you like things
God? For the regenerated souls, even in this
213
life, what gives us deepest satisfaction is
that which has to do with the glory of God. It is
an intimate, sublime, spiritual satisfaction, which does not
It can be found in the things of the world; not even in
the best; They are from another sphere, of inferior quality,
no matter how good they are. And this brings us to the aspiration
final.
4. The service of God.
He who loves God very intensely does not
content with a passive attitude of worship. We
we enjoy praising Him and hearing others praise Him; but
the supreme aspiration is service. what can i
do I for God. What can I give you that will please you?
And this aspiration must be fulfilled.
I would not like to read in the Apocalypse that in the
eternity the saved will always be sitting
listening to songs of angels, although that will be, without
doubt, a delightful part of our future life;
but I like to read the text: "His servants will serve him"
(Revelation 22:3). And according to Ephesians 3:10, we will serve him by glorifying him. We will have something to do in the
immense heaven of God..., something that will glorify him and us
will make you eternally happy. This is the end we hope for, the supreme, apotheotic, eternal end.
God knows our aspirations. What are
for this life? Which ones are for eternity? God
He will fulfill them in his day, even if he makes us
wait; in the same way that it will fulfill the final aspirations of our being.
214
"Seek first the Kingdom of God and its
justice – he tells us – and all other things will be unto you
added."

480 years ago, on October 12, 1942, a

From that historic day it seemed to Rodrigo to perceive

Make sure your eyes are not deceiving you, he exclaims

Approximately 1,900 years ago, a fisherman, son of Zebedee, made another discovery

long; put your attention on the love of God,
the heavenly Father, in the wonder that represents the

Can there be anything more admirable or better? Look,

3. The wonder of God's love
What kind of love is this? We can distinguish

1. Love earned.
Marital love is always based on

content:
(1st Corinthians 15:50-57)
No wonder life is considered a struggle.
From the moment we are born, the fight to survive begins.
At first it is not we alone who fight, because man is the most defenseless of the
animals; If we were left to our fate,
we would probably perish, but intelligence and
the love that God has given to our parents
provides for all our needs; not only present, but future. The newborn is subjected to
all kinds of attention and care, and he is vaccinated
against invisible enemies of the future.
As soon as the infant can help himself, he begins his
own fight for life: the child fights at school
to acquire the knowledge you need; fight
the young man with his passions and his disappointments; fight the
man in his business, to support his family;
The old man struggles with his ailments, and in the midst of
all this fight, there is no other perspective than the
final defeat: A disease stronger than us, against which, after fighting in vain, the
Science will declare itself powerless to help us…
224
Certainly life is a struggle that has no other
perspective that defeats!
Man is not satisfied with being defeated,
and, generation after generation, continues its efforts to know the secrets of Nature, to
live better and prolong human life as much as possible
existence. Our fight is easier today than in
the Stone Age or that in the Middle Ages, when
people perished helplessly by the tens of thousands before a plague... However, despite all
the advances of science, death seems to laugh at
us.
We do not yet have effective means of combating
cancer and leukemia; and if the day came when we had a remedy for all diseases, only
It would be a prolongation of the battle for life
for a few more years, since natural wear and tear
would give us up. The man without faith is defeated,
whether he wants to confess it or not.
1. A victorious defeated
But here we find a defeated
victorious that opens us perspective and hope
of a true victory.
The author of this writing was a defeated..., a
man whose life had been cut short, whose plans
were destroyed in their youth and were found
Being what I had never thought to be. In fact,
Saul of Tarsus was a young man dedicated to fighting for
225
the religion of their parents, when it appeared in their
days what he judged to be a religious plague;
some fanatics who said that a man who had
being crucified by Pontius Pilate was the Messiah. Without
Without a doubt, Saul thought that among the many bad and unjust sentences of the Roman procurator that
The Jews were sad, that one had been good. By
At least there would be no one who would bring excited crowds to the holy temple and cry out from its courts:
"Hypocritical scribes and Pharisees..."
But seven weeks pass and the fuss is made
much larger, since some supporters of the
executed saying: "God has made Him whom you crucified both Lord and Christ." and they quote
mysterious passages of the prophets and apply them to Him.
That inexplicable passage from the Psalms: "You will not let
my soul in Sheol, nor will you allow your saint to see
corruption", they say that it refers to Him, to Jesus of
Nazareth, which raised from the grave by the power
of God, is working new wonders...
Saul is enraged by such insolence and fighting, entering the houses to apprehend the
Christians and force them to blaspheme Christ. Until
that day on the road to Damascus he hears the
words: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
has to end by exclaiming: "Lord, what do you want?"
What do I do? Here is the defeated, handing over the
keys to his strength… As he himself confessed
years later: «I thought about doing many things
against the saints of Jerusalem..."
226
But that defeat is his greatest victory, because he allies himself with the "Victorious"; makes common cause
with Him and so, writing to the Corinthians, afternarrate the evidence of the resurrection of Jesus, and
to explain how he appeared to Cephas, to the twelve, to
more than five hundred disciples, to James and, ultimately, to him, his greatest enemy, he exclaims: "But
Thank God who gives us victory for him
Our Lord Jesus Christ." And what a victory! Hear him
(vv. 53-57).
2. Victory of sin
Note, however, a curious, remarkable fact
(vv. 55, 56). The main victory is not over
death, but about sin.
Death without sin is nothing in the world
spiritual. Have you seen a bee after having
Stung someone? It's an offensive fly
and tired. Have you had one in your hand?
stingless viper? It is a funny creature that
screws and unscrews and can be given to a child to
play without any danger.
Paul, the only man after Christ, who
knows well the secrets of the beyond, says that the
death, this terrible viper that attacks us and takes over us, that separates us from our loved ones, that transforms our body, this precious
body that we take care of with so much care, is a handful of dust and dry bones, it is not to be feared... It is
227
a stingless viper, we can laugh at it,
challenge her with impunity.
3. Victory over the fear of death
For this reason, while waiting to be judged by the madman
Nero, the arsonist of Rome, the murderer of his own courtiers and relatives, Paul writes about
life and death like two imaginary characters who come to his prison in Rome making propositions to him and he doesn't know what to choose. This is,
literally, the amazing word he uses:
"choose."
Life tells him: If you come with me you can come back
to Macedonia; you will see those brothers and children
spiritual people who love you so much by having parties and
receptions in your honor; you will preach to them again and
you will rejoice seeing the joy on their faces and news
saved souls Then you will make your desired trip to
Spain. Don't you want to come with me? Don't you want the
life? Pray to God that Nero has a moment
lucid on the day of your judgment and say like Gallio, the
sensible Spanish governor (Acts 18:14, 15).
But death tells him: It will only be a moment,
Pablo, don't be a coward. A slightly strong blow on

sting to him; had seen the sting of death

In Philippians 3:14 it is compared to a sports runner advancing on a wrong path; but

SERMîN XX
THE TRIUMPHAL CHANTIC
OF THE CHRISTIAN FIGHTER
(1st Timothy 4:6 to 8)
Preached on the occasion of the funeral of the notable
Spanish preacher, pastor of the Baptist Church
from Barcelona, Don Ambrosio Celma,
on January 8, 1944.
It is said of the swan, that it sings when it feels it arrives.
death. This phenomenon took place in the apostle
Paul. But his parting words do not sound like
requiem, but to glory. It is because the old apostle
He could look back on his past with as much satisfaction as

1. His past
a) I have fought the good fight.  The life of everything

10:34) and the experience of the great apostle declares it

(Ephesians 6:12). The life of a person is to the maximum extent.
minister of the Gospel. How many conflicts did he have to

Christ has called us into fierce conflict with the

ruins or remorse like that which some warriors have felt at the hour of death, but everything

Some good causes have had to be defended with bad battles, but it is a great satisfaction
fight for Christ, as Paul did, sacrificing
only oneself in favor of others (2 Timothy 2:10).
As William Booth wrote in the famous
phrase that gave rise to its admirable institution, "the
"Church is an army of salvation." It is not necessary
238
wear a uniform to be a soldier of the same. Paul
He never wore it, but he was perhaps the most notable strategist in the centuries-long struggle that ended with
the effective defeat against the sin and evil that exists
in the world.
What place do we occupy in this titanic company?Are we soldiers of good, active, determined, conquerors? There are Christians who confuse their church with a hospital. Eternal spiritual patients
They want to be pampered and cared for, instead of being willing to fight for Christ and care for others.
These will not be able to sing a song of triumph to the

b) I have finished the race. Any race not

those who have lived in
the joy of daily communion with God (Genesis 5:
24). This is how the brother whose departure we remember finished it, working to glorify his Master until

How will we finish it? If we are faithful, there will be a double reason for joy: on the one hand,

239
c) I have kept the faith.  Which? The reception of Jesus Christ (1st Corinthians 11:23). "The faith once given to the

Christ Jesus. This is how our beloved brother kept it;
He never deviated from the fundamentals. And so we must

2. Your present
The end of a life is always miserable and sad,

pleasure. Not "my end", the end of everything.
c). Bring the cape and the books.  Try to take care of the

eternity. A cold and sick body cannot
day to be easily employed in the service of Christ,
writing or speaking to the guardians. Our
body is the wonderful working instrument that
God has given us. Let's take care of it carefully; let's use it well until the last moment and leave it without
regret when God calls us.
3. Your future
The crown of righteousness is laid up for me. What beautiful security! Where did you receive it from? It couldn't be one

that he followed a new path in religion, precisely the one they called "heresy." Only by true revelation could I have obtained so certain
hope that ancient enemy of the Christian faith.
He had seen the crown, he had received the promise

We must distinguish that this is not about salvation, entry into Heaven, won by Christ and

There can be no crown without entry into the palace.
The apostle had both. I had lived like that
so that he was sure that the judgment of his
241
works, done by the "just Judge", could not help but

same?
4. His generous warning
The noble and loving apostle was not content with
be crowned him. He consoled himself with the hope thatmany more would share his privilege. You wish that
be so. This is why he formulates his faithful warning: "and do not

a) He is saved by Christ. He is not afraid of meeting him. know

b) He will be an active Christian who will work to

c) He will live blamelessly (Jude 24). For
be found without offense on the day of Christ (Philippians
1:10).
d) He will not fear death either, which is another way
to join the waiting Savior (See anecdote
Moody's death.)
How sweet is the voice of brotherly love in these
solemn moments of farewell! With feet in
the thresholds of eternity, think fondly

242
In the same way that the great apostle said,
our beloved brother would tell us that he has already entered

career, "try to make your vocation and choice firm...", work and fight, overcoming the
difficulties. You can do something more to
polish your crown; do it, while
you have time Soon we will meet to enjoy together the same good that the Lord's abundant grace will bestow "on all who love his
coming." Amen.
ANECDOTES
JUSTINE MARTYR, AND THE PROCONSUL
When Justin Martyr was presented, with six others

–Do you suppose that if you were whipped and your heads were cut off, you would go up to heaven to be rewarded?
To which Justino, coming forward, replied:
–I do not suppose it, but I know it, and I am fully
convinced of it.
The same day, after being flogged, they were led to the torture where they died glorifying God.
243
THE DEATH OF VOLTAIRE
Voltaire was, without a doubt, the most talented atheist than
world has known. He wrote 250 publications, the largest
some of them against Christianity. It is logical to think that
such an intelligent man should remain faithful to his
convictions at the hour of death. But it wasn't like that. If

To God forgiveness for your sins. He said it had been

Jesus Christ!" to burst almost immediately into blasphemies. His doctor and nurse Marchal de Richelieu
They left the room because they said they couldn't see a
such a horrible death. It has been rightly said that the time
of death is the moment of truth.
MOODY'S DEATH
Mr. Moody died as he had lived. I used to say this
great servant of the Lord:
–Someday you will read in the newspapers that D. L. Moody
has died; don't believe it. When they say I'm dead
I will be more alive than ever.
It is actually very easy to say this when you enjoy
good health, but it is a fact that Mr. Moody, in the
last moments of his life, he looked death in the face
face to face without any fear.
On his last day on earth, in the morning, very
early, his son Bill, who was watching him, heard him whisper something
and leaning down he was able to capture these words:
244
–The earth recedes, the sky opens, God is with me
calling.
Uneasy, Bill called the other members of the
family
–No, no, dad; “You're not so bad,” his son told him.
He opened his eyes and seeing himself surrounded by his family,
said:
–I have already been inside the doors. I have seen the
children's faces. (He was referring to two grandchildren who
little had died.)
Shortly afterward he lost consciousness again; but of
Again, coming to his senses, he opened his eyes and said:
–Is this death? This is not bad! There is no such valley
gloomy This is bliss; this is sweet, this
It's the glory.
With a broken heart, his daughter told him:
–Dad, don't leave us!
"Oh, Emilia," replied the dying man, "I don'tI refuse to live. If God wants me to live, I will live; but yes
God calls me, I must get up and go.
A little later, someone tried to wake him up,
but he answered in a low voice:
–God is calling me. Don't bother me to
let it come back. This is the day of my coronation. long ago
that I expected it.
And so his spirit flew to the presence of God, to
receive the crown of his glory.

content:
THE TWO PARADISES
(Genesis 2:8-18
Revelation 21:1—22:6)
The Bible begins with a paradise and ends with
another. Both are places of happiness. The first was
prepared for the natural man; the second, for
the redeemed man.
Skeptics mock the Eden story, since
They say it's a myth. Let's think about it calmly.
There is a highly intelligent Being, as observed in nature, which was for centuries
preparing the conditions of the land to put
in it all kinds of living beings, and finally man,
the only one who can understand, admire and thank the works of his Creator. If the man was the work
summit of Creation, if the world had been prepared for it, is it not natural that it was introduced
In some kind of museum, where he could learn sooner and more easily what was good for him about the home he was going to inhabit? (Genesis 2:9). a son
of God, because of his intelligence and spirit, could not be
treated as irrational. The cave paintings
246
prove that troglodyte man was much more
than a brute. On the other hand, ancient history is
full of traditions of Paradise: the «Golden Age»
of the classical poets, the "Garden of the Hesperides",
etc. They all agree that it was lost.
But the Bible ends with another paradise regained
for man, far superior in all its aspects.
It is very interesting to consider their contrasts:
1. The first paradise was earthly
Its location in Western Asia is detailed. He was, therefore, exposed to the vicissitudes
of the earth, and was destroyed, it seems, by the
Flood.
The second paradise is heavenly.  It is also detailed

the highest place in the universe (Revelation
21:2).
From there it descends towards the earth. Possibly the
lifts it, tearing it from the solar orbit, to carry it,
once renewed by fire (2 Peter 3:12, 13),
for the immense universe of God that is the inheritance
of the redeemed, as the apostle says: "Everything is
yours. However, there is a place in the Universe
specific that is the homeland of the saints, of which
Jesus speaks in John 14:1-3 and 17:24: "The city of
God", "the heavenly Jerusalem", the true and definitive Paradise.
247
2. There was night
This is necessary because of the fragility of
our bodies, which require rest; but it means almost half a life lost.
In the second there is no night, because there is no sun;
God himself is his light (Revelation 22:5). The
activity is without rest and without fatigue. The joy,
the praises and receptions of those who bring to this
blessed place "the glory and honor of all the nations" of the universe, is unceasing (Revelation 21:26).
3. Satan entered
(Genesis 3:1). The great enemy of God, envious of the happiness of our parents, introduced into
his soul pure distrust and ambition, both
great evils of the world. Why do they fight
men? Satan has always managed humanity by pulling these two reins at will.
In the second, Satan is excluded (Revelation
20:10). This means that there will be no more thoughts
of distrust towards God and towards others, nor more
ambition, for there will be no sin. (See anecdote
The two angels.)
4. The pain entered
(Genesis 3:17). The condition of the world seems
which was varied after the fall and because of it
(Romans 8:20-22). "Thorns and thistles" in the earth,
248
fierce instincts in animals, bacteria that produce diseases of which new forms seem to be produced. The pain increases as the sin progresses. We are not happier than
the patriarchs, even though we surpass them in
so many things.
In the second, the pain will be removed.  All the
reasons for moral and physical pain will disappear: At
death, illness, poverty and sin, they are
He will call them “the first things,” regarding them only as a sad memory of the past (Revelation 21:4).
5. The curse enteredThe only one who has the power to turn his word into reality, had to pronounce a sentence of
bad. No one but Him can do it (Psalm 109:28).
It is audacity for mere humans to pretend
throw curses and more in the Christian Era (Matthew
6:44 and Romans 12:14). In many respects the results of the divine curse still remain.
in the world.
In the second there will be no curse, because there will be no
no reason for her among perfect beings. The
last curse will have been pronounced against the
reprobates, and it will be the final in the Universe.
249
6. There was shame
(Genesis 3:10). Man cannot suffer God
nor to his word when he does evil. (Cite the
examples of Cain fleeing from the presence of Jehovah
and of Joakim burning the book of the Law.) For this reason
The Christian must avoid sin, because it is a temple of
God through the Holy Spirit.
In the second paradise there will be trust (Revelation 22:4). Despite living in the presence of God
will not be afraid of his omniscience, because nothing
may be found reprehensible in its happy inhabitants. We must start here to live this kind of
life.
7. The entrance was closed
God did not immediately remove paradise from
land, but closed it (Genesis 3:22-24). It was for the
first sinners a testimony of happiness
lost.
The second paradise is always open (Revelation 21:25). This amazed Juan, accustomed to
see carefully walled ancient cities
and closed. But there is no danger of enemies entering the heavenly city. Its open doors are
symbol of freedom.
250
8. It ended
(Genesis 3:24). We do not know how long the happiness of the first paradise lasted, but it is assumed that it was
very brief, since Adam's first son was already born
out of Eden.
The second will have no end (Revelation 22:5). It has been
said that only the eternal of happiness is happiness.
The more precious and pleasant a thing is, the worse it is to lose it. The best thing about heaven is that it will be ours
forever home.
Do we have a place in the second paradise? It's there
our treasure and our hope. Any class
of good outside of this is a deception and must come to
soon be a disappointment.
Heaven, which some consider an illusion
mystical, is the only truly objective reality. Christ affirmed his existence with his authority without
the same (John 14:2). Thinking about it rationally, there is no
empire without capital, just as there is no body without a head.
The universe cannot be without a center. Christ us
assures what a high and blessed place ours will be.
eternal habitation if we join Him by faith. wine
to open the doors of the upper Paradise for us with his
expiatory death; is the second Adam (Romans
5:18, 19). His greatest satisfaction on the same cross was
offer the dying thief immediate entry to the
new Eden. Is Heaven open for you?
251

A preacher wanting to demonstrate the condition

another to sweep their streets, they would both feel satisfied
to fulfill the will of God. But what would happen if the
command was given to two men of equal status?
It would rise immediately in the heart of the least
favored a storm of envy and resentment. I have
here the sin.
