content:
EXISTENCE OF THE SOUL
(Psalm 8;
Matthew 10:28 and 16:26)
Introduction
(See anecdote Nietzche and the park guard.)
Certainly the questions: What in the world am I?
What role do human beings occupy in the immense Universe? Why do we exist? By virtue of
What can we realize about our existence?
These are questions that cannot help but be asked.
every thinking man.
David knew nothing of what science has told us
revealed about the greatness of the Universe; without
However, comparing the smallness of man with
the things he knew and saw, and in a fit of
inspiration, exclaims: "What is man that
have remembrance of him, and the son of man so that
"Do you visit him?" Certainly, considered as matter,
the most handsome and robust man is very little
In a world of forty million meters
circumference and billions of quintals of weight.
253
But David sees in him much more than a compound
of matter: an angel in a carnal case (v. 5) and Jesus,
who knew things better than David, puts it into
highest esteem (Matthew 16:26). Because? The man
is a spiritual being that feels, meditates, knows, loves,
lives now and will live for eternity, and God, who is
Also spirit but infinite, it cares about man more than any other material being. Doesn't look
its smallness, but its faculties.
Suppose a rich father sees his house burned down.
palace, in which a little son of a few years is found.
He will not appreciate the death of his son as the loss
of 30 or 35 kilos of matter that is carbonized. your son
It has come from him, it carries his image, something of his character,
and faculties capable of developing; all of which,
They do not own their palace, nor their furniture, nor their machines. For this reason he will throw himself into the flames crying: "Save my son."
1. Man bears the image of God
All men bear the image of God
invisible. We have powers that only God can
have and that are not found in other beings. studying
nature we discover the traces of an Intelligent Being endowed with will, initiative, wisdom and immense power, which has organized with
admirable design and foresight the Universe that
surrounds These undeniable qualities that we recognize
in the Creator, we find them in ourselves.
254
It could not be said of an animal that it is "the image of
God." This one has a wonderful body and brain, but
His powers do not correspond to those that should be
in Divinity.
It has been observed that animals do everything
attracted by physical sensations: hunger, thirst, desire
sexual, etc., or by an inner impulse that
It comes from God as a general law and is called instinct.
There is no intellectual initiative in them, nor
progress. The bird has never known how to invent a
cover to preserve its nest from the rain. The rabbit
It has never thought of forming rooms in its burrow. The bee builds a honeycomb that leaves even the wisest geometer amazed, but it is the work of the species - that is, of God, by the law of instinct -, not its own.
own.
As wonderful as instinct is, it does not reveal personality. Swallows with larger heads or
smaller, with more or less gray matter, their children build the same. But a man doesn't do
than another man. The paintings of Velázquez or the
Bach's music cannot be devised by other men.
The human spirit not only has facilities to
learn, but can create. The simplest worker is a creator of models in his mind, to which
It takes shape very quickly if you have materials at your disposal. Who does this little creator look like?
the earth, but to his Father, the supreme Creator of the
heavens?
255
2. Man has moral virtues
We have discovered that God is good by examining the works of Nature. What seem like evils
They are nothing but inevitable accidents, some aimed at greater good. In countless details the
Creator has tried to put elements of happiness
for all his creatures that reveal his character
kind. The Bible tells us about the love of God inanother higher ground, that of Redemption (John
3:16). The book of
Revelation and that of Nature.
Man created in the image of God preserves,
though half obliterated by sin, these hallmarks of their origin. He has feelings of compassion, kindness, tenderness – not only towards his offspring,
like animals by instinct, but towards all
other beings. Because? Because God is love.
For the same reason we have moral conscience.
Who, in fact, is this self that rises up against
the other self to judge and condemn him in our inner being, even when the reason for the rebuke
Is it something extremely favorable to ourselves?
Is it a nerve that reprimands other nerves in our body? Is it a muscle that reacts against
other muscles? Is it, in a word, matter condemning matter?
The animal is perfectly satisfied
with satisfying his instincts, but the man feels
tormented by his conscience if that satisfied256
tion is to the detriment of a neighbor. Because? because
God is justice, and we carry something within us
of that divine attribute. Even the most relaxed, most degenerate and cruel men sometimes have
some trait of nobility. These vestiges that
remains of the "image of God" prove our
superior origin, and, as a logical consequence, a
destiny higher than that presented to us by the philosophers of "Nothing."
3. The soul is not the brain
Our self is not that poor body that serves us
of room. Many confuse the being with the instrument, but the material instrument cannot be
efficient cause of thought. How can a vibration of the eardrum become a feeling?
of hate or love, of pleasure or sadness? who
Are you happy or sad? The neurons, that is, the brain cells? No, these are mere transmitting agents; Well, as psychologists say, we cannot imagine the brain as a producer and receiver of images that no one receives, that no one collects.
and interprets. "I am sad with the news" cannot
translate "a series of images inside me
brain have become sad. Without the "I", the most
admirable operations of the most perfect computer of the brain are nothing, nor mean anything.
The brain is, indeed, the office of the soul; and
It is wonderful in its configuration and organization.
257
There the soul archives its memories. But there must be
something more than a file. For example, when
we forget one thing and we have it, as they say, "on the tip of our tongue", someone remembers that other details are there, and has no
them. Perhaps the name of a city, or a
person.
Who is the one who possesses the memory of the event, or
of the thing, but it lacks the lost detail and sends it
search within your physical archive of neurons?
Who is the one who "knows" that he "should know"? It is without
doubts the extraphysical "I" that we call "soul."
We have every reason to believe that the body is only the instrument of the soul, and certainly
some one is the most suitable for her. A body of
bird or fish, endowed with spirit, would have had
great difficulties in putting his thoughts into practice. Other beings, very similar to us
in physical body, but not in intelligence (the monkeys),
They seem to have been put to prove to us that the
immense difference does not consist in bodily shapes or structures, but in something extraphysical superior to
the matter
4. The soul is immortal
a) Logic tells us so. It is not material; and if matter is not lost, but transformed, something must
happen with the soul. If made in the image of God,
and God is eternal, it is fitting that she be eternal as well.
258
b) Gradation in Nature shows us this.
We observe three kingdoms in it: mineral, vegetal
and animal, at whose summit man is found.
But if death destroyed us completely it would be the
abrupt return from the superior to the inferior, from the intelligent spirit to the dust of the earth. what objectwould the entire Creation be in that case? But if he
world and the universe are rooms to educate
moral and eternal beings, the request of the
Creator for the benefit of his children.
c) Our conscience tells us. Where did it come from
to man the idea of immortality if God does not
revealed? It would be too cruel a mockery to give us the
desire and not satisfy it. The fact that the man
Have you thought if you have an immortal soul, it is the best
proof that it has it, since no animal is
such a doubt has occurred to you.
d) Christ tells us.  The great revealer of God
to humanity he affirms: "Do not fear those who kill
the body” (Matthew 10:26). "God is not the God of the dead... for all live in him" (Luke 20:38).
Immortality is the key why the N.T.
solves all moral enigmas. The solution of
all the injustices we suffer, and the most glorious of hopes. What does it matter in such a case?
illness and old age? (2 Corinthians 5:1). What does death itself matter? Philippians 1:21).
259
5. The soul can be lost
No spirit stained by sin can
enter the Life where the harmony of perfection of the children of God reigns. This is the great danger
about which Christ came to warn us (John 3:15
and Luke 13:28).
It is the most terrible loss because it is irreparable.
All loss of life, interest or health
can be remedied. But we only have one
soul: if we lose it, when God puts it to the test,
is lost forever. (See the anecdote Irreparable loss.)
We are not able to define in detail
which means perdition, but it must be something quite terrible, when the Word of God decided to
incarnate and suffer so much in order to free ourselves from
such a tragedy. To avoid it, it is essential,
However, not only his sacrifice, but our acceptance of it. Hence so many exhortations of the Son
of God to repentance and faith (Mark 1:15 and
John 5:40).
6. The soul can be saved
In another more modern, less theological-scholastic phrase, "he can fulfill his destiny." According to
Hebrews 2:10, the Creator had a great purpose
from the beginning of the race: "bring to glory
many children» (see anecdote Two ways of imagining260
us to God). We can defeat God's purpose
and lose ourselves, or adjust to it and save ourselves. As?
Accepting the means of salvation provided by Him.
God sent Christ to die for our sins
to be able to forgive ourselves with justice, and to ourselves
time move our hearts taking us back to
a voluntary and joyful obedience, obedience
out of love, out of gratitude for the affection that his sacrifice
has risen in our hearts. Will we do it?
Will we correspond to the sublime purpose that God
has it had to save our souls?
7. What does the salvation of the soul mean?
The human soul, because it is spiritual and therefore
immortal, has unsuspected possibilities, unimaginable from this confinement of mortal flesh in which
we meet You can see the greatness of such
purpose in John 17:24; John 14:1-3 and Ephesians 1:1112. (Brief glossary of such texts according to time and
the circumstances.)
We still have time to save our soul
immortal. Let us heed the words of Christ.
Let's take the matter seriously. Let's give it the value that
has. The worst of the condemnation will be this: "I could
to be happy and I wasn't, I could save myself and I condemned myself.
May God grant that none of those present have
what to say
261
ANECDOTES
NIETZSCHE AND THE PARK GUARD
It is told of the great atheist philosopher Nietzsche – who
after having written substantial books he finished his
life in a madhouse – that one day, while sitting in a park in Berlin, the
closing time. A guard, taking him for a traveler
homeless man who was trying to spend the night in the park,
He approached him and said:
–Have you not heard the closing siren? Tell me:
Who are you? Where does it come from? Where is he going?
To which Nietzsche replied:–This is precisely what I have been wondering for 40 years, and I still haven't come to know it.
Could you tell me?
IRREPARABLE LOSS
A man, desirous of acquiring fortune, sold
everything he had to move to California. There he worked for 16 years without knowing rest, searching for
coveted gold dust, eventually managing to gather
a great fortune, which (at that time when there was no
current banking facilities existed) became
a valuable diamond that he intended to sell in Europe
for an amount that would make him rich for the rest of his life.
lives. But one day when I was showing the precious
jewel to some friends of traveled, a movement of the ship
caused him to lose his balance, with such bad luck that the
262
The diamond slipped from his hands and ended up in the sea.
What a terrible moment!
But the loss of the soul is worse.
TWO WAYS TO IMAGINE GOD
Someone has said that considering the wonderful dispositions of Nature and the failure that
represents death for life, especially in what
the human being refers, or we must imagine
God like a child who blows soap bubbles for the
pleasure to see how they fall apart, or do we have to consider
to God as a father who is raising a family
for Eternity.
Which of the two concepts is more worthy of the Creator,
and above all, from a very wise Creator like the one who gave us
reveal the works of Nature?
263

content:
THE UNEQUALED INVITATION
(Matthew 11:28-30)
One day when Jesus was teaching the people, some officers sent by the priests came to arrest him. Wishing to justify his action,
They were waiting to hear him utter some compromising word; but instead of reaching out,
They returned to their bosses with the answer: "He never spoke
man just like this man” (John 7:46).
Those ministers were certainly right.
What man has ever dared to utter words like those in our text? (v. 28). However, was it necessary for them to be pronounced? Do they respond to a need of the human race?
It has been said that man is an eternal seeker of happiness, which moves away from him as
that your capacity to enjoy grows. The child of few
weeks he feels happy with very little, but his
Difficulties grow to the same extent that their faculties develop. Upon entering puberty,
expands your capacity to enjoy; a smile of being
beloved makes him happy; But how many disappointments too! He comes to marriage with the hope that
264
absolute possession of what you love will make you happy, and
Not even in the best cases is this the case. And the man dies with
the hope of being happier a little later,
for when he seems to have almost reached his ideal,
a breakdown in health or fortune or the loss of a
loved one collapses his castle of happiness. From there
the need that Humanity has had and will have
always comforting. So much so that in Greece and
Rome there were professional comforters, who came to provide their services to afflicted homes,
reading passages from the classics and then presenting
your bill, like our doctors or lawyers.
But the great Comforter is offered in this text
to do for free what no one has been able to do effectively.
It has been said that there are three main reasons for
unhappiness for men:
• Physical pain.
• Moral penalties.
• The fear of death.
That physical pain disturbs happiness is not difficult
try it.
That there are pains equal to or worse than physical pain
In the domains of the soul it is very evident: the
remorse, anxiety, shame, fear,
They hurt us more deeply than the pains of
body. So much so that the soul can overcome
to physical pain, as has happened with the great saints and martyrs, but there is no remedy for the
pains of the soul Today we can more easily
265
never free ourselves from physical pain; but there is no narcotic for remorse, for regret; there is not
remedy for death. However, the humble carpenter from Nazareth appears and exclaims: The remedy
from evil, from pain, from heartbreak, from
fear and uncertainty of the afterlife, it is me.
"Come to Me, you who are labored and heavy laden, and I will make you
rest."
Note that he does not offer advice, but rather his person.
This cannot be said by a mere mortal. because
No one can care for all his fellow men, not even in relieving physical pain, and mostly
because no one is capable of removing certain pains from the
soul Humanity had never heard a claim
similar. These words would be the most eminent madness if they were not uttered by the one who said them.
But is not Christ the wisest, the most prudent, the
most perfect of men?
1. Christ, Comforter of physical pain
This unique man began by alleviating the
body pains. There was no sick or sore
will not find comfort in Him. His miracles are public
and undeniable. Their own enemies attribute them to
anything: magic, pact with the devil, etc.,
but they do not deny them. (See the anecdote The statement
of the Talmud.) With this he demonstrated his power to alleviate
spiritual evils (Luke 5:24). Even outside the
Gospels there are historical clues of reality
266
of his supernatural power. (See the anecdote Cuadrato's declaration.)
Even without going to the days of his ministry, prayerof faith in his name has often worked miracles of healing, although these cannot be the rule
absolute because such kind of divine intervention,
carried out constantly, although it would greatly increase the volume of faith, it would not make it
the quality that God desires (John 20:29) and would remove the
opportunity to manifest heroic virtues: patience, trust and love against any test. More
If it doesn't take away the pain in all cases, it takes away the sting.
of pain when he reveals to us the great secret that he senses
our conscience, that God is love and does not consent
the evil of its degree, but so that it results
some good in our favor for eternity. This
It takes away the moral part of the pain, it softens it, it makes it
friendly
2. Christ, Comforter of moral evils
Of them is Christ the Physician par excellence, since
that almost all have their origin and cause in sin.
Fear, remorse, anxiety and the evils caused by hatred and envy all have their cause in the transgression of the divine will. who
came to take away sin came to destroy all its
consequences. The doctrine of Redemption is the
supreme remedy for conscience. There is no reason to grieve over sin; not because it's a thing
267
light, but because although it is horrible before God, it has
been atoned for on the cross of Calvary, where the Comforter of men suffered the punishment so that
we could have forgiveness and peace. This
doctrine gives rest even to the most submerged soul
in sin, leaving it light and suitable for all
good work (See the anecdote The Conversion of the Russian Bandit.)
3. Christ, Comforter of death
In this aspect Jesus Christ is unique. nobody
has spoken of death and the afterlife in the form
that He spoke. Plato's dialogues on the immortality of the soul are a model of logic and good
sense, but there is not in them the firm and authoritative language that only he who came from the world could use
of immortality. No prophet, wise man or philosopher
has ever dared to say: «I am the resurrection
and life", "Do you not want to come to Me so that you may have
life?", "In my Father's house many mansions
there is. The afterlife hope that Christ offers
It is not a painful ascension through innumerable reincarnations; a vision of almost endless advances and setbacks, but a powerful hand that
extends to free us from our moral misery and
elevate us to the highest dignities in heaven.
This hope made Paul exclaim: "I would like to be
unbound and be with Christ" and was also the one who
He put flowers and myrtle on the foreheads of the maidens
268
Christians who were going to be devoured in the circuses of
Rome, as if it were your wedding day. She has
removed the fear of death from everyone who
possesses. (See the anecdote Moving Poetry.)
4. The conditions for divine comfort
Let us note that to obtain such rest and privilege it is essential to meet two conditions:
• Feeling burdened and fatigued.
• Go directly to the Giver of rest.
Perhaps you object to not feeling in the conditions
that the Savior claims; But even if you are not desperate, look, reader, to the depths of your conscience.
«Are you happy? Have all your wishes come true?
Don't you feel the slightest remorse or fear?
Will the good that you enjoy today be eternal? If you can't
respond affirmatively to all of these
You ask, you need Christ. There really isn't
man or woman completely happy without Him. Many who
They seem happy, they only try to forget that
They are unhappy. (See the anecdote The Prisoner and the
concertina.)
5. The conditions for complete happiness
There is a strange reiteration between the verses
28 and 29, but this is perhaps the best proof of the wisdom
divine strength of the one who uttered such extraordinary
words.
Verse 28 shows us the divine factor of
our happiness, what Christ does for us
when we turn to Him, and the 29th our part. We
says that we can be more or less happy, findmore or less moral rest depending on whether we comply with the
teachings of the Savior. To be completely happy, two conditions must be met:
1. Take my yoke upon you
There are those who believe they are happier accepting the
salvation without the yoke; believe without visibly joining
to Christ and his Church. But it is a big mistake. confess
Christ increases spiritual joy. He is poor and
sad Christianity that of those who try to bring
hidden his faith.
It is almost a shame that Christ himself has
They must defend their cause by affirming that their yoke is easy.
We know it well, dear Savior! how little
you demand of yours in this time of grace! More
how much you deserve! We should well tell him: Even if your yoke were a thousand times heavier, we would gladly bear it, Lord, for love of you.
2. Learn from Me, for I am meek and humble in
        heart.
There are others who easily accept the yoke; some perhaps thoughtlessly, but they are little
willing to learn and imitate the virtues of Psalm270
vador. But absolute happiness is not possible without
make our life completely similar to that of our
Teacher and Example. We could be very happy in
hope and very little in the present reality yes
We live far from Christian virtues. Christ
He wants to make us happy here and there. How much more
we would be if we knew how to receive setbacks
and the offenses with the meekness and humility of the
Savior!
This is how it must be, in a real, not apparent way; by
this adds "humble of heart." He knew well
Lord, much of the humility of those who would profess to be your disciples would be hypocrisy. just
humility of heart makes the person entirely happy
who owns it.
Who doesn't want to be happy in life? Do not look for happiness where it is not. Go to Christ; receive him
by Salvador; confess his Name even if it is
facing disgrace; imitate him in his virtues
morals, and your happiness will begin now so as not to
never end.
ANECDOTES
THE AFFIRMATION OF THE TALMUD
The Talmud, written by the Jews enemies of Christ
in the first centuries of our Era, declares that Jesus
of Nazareth worked miracles, healed the lame and maimed, gave sight
271
blind and even raised the dead, but it was by arts
magical things he had learned in Egypt. For us,
men of the 20th century, who know that there are no magical arts capable of performing such wonders, the confession of
his enemies is one of the proofs we have that
Jesus Christ was truly the Son of God.
THE SQUARE DECLARATION
Cuadrato, who wrote in the first half of the century
II, has left us this testimony: «The works of our
Salvador were always visible, because they were real;
of this kind are both those whom he healed and those whom he resurrected,
which were seen not only when they were healed
and resurrected, but after his departure and for quite some time
time after it, so much so that some of those who
known have reached our time. (Eusebius,
Ecclesiastical History, Book 4, chap. III.)
THE CONVERSION OF THE RUSSIAN BANDIT
Pablo Tichomiroff emigrated with his family to Siberia,
where his parents died of cholera. After some painful experiences, he joined a gang of
thieves who taught him to steal and kill. One day they murdered two men, stealing from them, among other things, a
New Testament and a book titled The Voice of Faith. Tichomiroff read Romans 3 that same night and was
deeply moved, seeing his portrait in those words. On the first page of the N.T. found this
written: «May 15, 1898, the day of my conversion to
272
Lord, of my repentance and new birth. In
This day He forgave my sins and washed me with His blood. He barely slept all night.
The next day, the bandits argued about the
books, finally deciding that they should be read aloud.
One of the bandits, named Solowjew, remembered words he had heard his mother read. after a month
reading, this companion and Pablo decided to stoptheir criminal practices, and when they told their companions of their purpose, five others agreed to leave their
life of sin and surrender to the authorities.
The governor was astonished and began to read with his
wife the book that wrought such a wonderful transformation,
resulting in the conversion of the governor.
Tichomiroff preached to the prisoners and the chaplain of
The Greek Church asked that he be removed from these.
Then he dedicated himself to announcing the Gospel to his guardians. A year later, the seven thieves were sentenced to ten years of hard labor. The trial was a
magnificent exposition of the Gospel, because in their statements they did not stop glorifying Jesus Christ. They were
sent to various prisons and before separating
They solemnly promised to be honest before
of God, and witnesses of Christ wherever they went
sent.
Tichomiroff and Solowjew were sent beyond the
Lake Baikal. After two years of being there it was observed that many turbulent prisoners had changed
of conduct. A few years later they were pardoned
on the occasion of a national holiday. When they said goodbye to them in the concentration camp, everyone cried.
They returned to Russia on foot, visiting many religious groups.
yentes through the towns where they passed. In a population
where they preached, there was a spiritual awakening and
many were converted. Back to Sosnowka, his town
native, Paul's evangelistic work aroused the opposition of the Russian priests, for which he was arrested
again, but this time for the sake of Christ. He was eventually banished to Siberia, where he continued his work.
evangelical
On the first page of the stolen New Testament,
which was the cause of his conversion, Paul wrote:
«Forgive me for the love of Christ, beloved brother. I
I killed you when I myself was dead in my sins.
The Lord has forgiven me and raised me to newness
of life. Your premature death took me, not only to
me, but to many other sinners and murderers, to life
eternal. For this I thank God, my Lord and yours.
Amen".
They were the words of repentance from a Paul
Russian to an unknown Russian Stephen.
MOVING POETRY
The following poetry was found in the vest of a
American soldier killed in one of the battles of
the invasion of France:
Listen, oh God, I never thought about You,
But I want to greet you, my Lord.
They told me that You did not exist;
foolish of me, that's what I thought.
I never noticed your great works
274
and last night, from the crater of a shell,
I saw your universe, beautiful, starry,
and I understood that I had been deceived.
I don't know, my God, if you will receive me
If I come to You, you will rather understand,
Lord, what a strange find to have found
in this hell your light so admirable.
I don't have to tell you much, my Father;
It's just that I'm glad to have met you.
At the touch of dawn, Lord! there will be offensive,
but I no longer fear because you are with me.
The sign, my God, I must leave.
How sorry I am, oh God! And this is the reason:
It was so sweet talking to you here!
But I stop, and I remain like this, I tell you:
The fight today will be cruel, bloody;
Maybe today I will knock on your door.
Although I was never, Lord, your friend,
Won't you let me come with me?
If I have to come to your door today,
Won't you have it open for me, Lord?
I'm here crying. Don't you see it?
I am crying, my God, I regret it.
I cry with joy when I talk to you;
of the joy of feeling like your friend.
I must leave, my God! I have to leave,
Not even a single moment does he grant me duty.
Goodbye, Lord, goodbye or see you soon.
275
How strange that I no longer fear death!
BRING ME A CONCERTINA!
A young man sentenced to death, when offered to ask
whatever I wanted on the last night, as usual,
He said, "Bring me a concertina." And with her he was trying to distract his grief until the very moment of taking him to the scaffold.
Did the concertina make the unfortunate man happier?
True happiness would have been obtained with the pardon.
Christ wants to make you really happy by giving you pardonof God. Don't you want to receive it?
276
SERMIN XXIV
CHANGE OF ROWS
(1st Chronicles 12:16-18)
The story of the transfer to David of the first
Saul's volunteers become a beautiful illustration of the souls that desert the ranks of the Devil
to enroll in those of Christ. Let's consider:
1. Saul's army
It had a lot of resemblance to that of the Enemy of
the souls
a) It was big. Hundreds of thousands of Israelites followed Saul (1 Samuel 15:4), the only visible king. A
David, far away and hidden, no one saw him. of the same
Thus, the ranks of the Devil are well nourished (Matthew
7:13). The crowds obey their king without realizing
account. Why is this side so numerous?

Model; He who knew how to say: «The will of my
"Father, I always do," and he could hear from the heights
that voice that was once heard in the Jordan, but
that will one day resonate in the heights, applied to you
and to me, if we have been his disciples and imitators:
301
«These are my children, loved, accepted and united to the
Word, my Only Begotten by faith and love. Therefore,
They are loved by God.
Then it will be our glorification, if we have
fulfilled his five conditions, as disciples,
redeemed, lovers, active workers and imitators of
our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
ANECDOTES
KING THEODOSIUS
AND THE PATRIARCH OF CONSTANTINOPLEThe emperor Theodosius being very inclined to
Arianism, an audience was requested by the Patriarch of
Constantinople, champion of the ancient faith in complete
and eternal divinity of Christ.
In those days the monarch used to make sit
in his public audiences to the crown prince so that
trained in the issues and problems of government. At
When the Patriarch entered the royal room he made a deep impression.
He bowed to the emperor, but, departing from the usual etiquette, he paid no attention to the prince.
–How dare you…? the sovereign exclaimed indignantly, pointing to the heir's chair.
“Do not be indignant, Your Majesty,” replied the patriarch.
All my respects are for the prince; but I wanted to make you feel what will be the attitude of the Sovereign of all
things towards those who despise the Only Begotten, who is the
radiance of his glory and the very image of his substance.
302
THE JEW OF BARCELONA AND THE MARTYRS OF HITLER
Discussing with a Jew from Barcelona about the messianism of Christ, he told me:
–I don't know why Christians give so much importance
to Jesus Christ, when millions of other Jews have suffered
worse and longer agonies in Hitler's concentration camps, and no one takes care of them.
I instantly tried to make him see that those were
unhappy, worthy of the greatest appreciation and pity; but they were
simple men, who could do nothing more than
suffer; They had no power to free themselves from the hands of
his minions; but Christ had shown to have all the
power; He did not deny it when he was tried by the Sanhedrin,
and yet he submitted to the ridicule provoked by his
words and the terrible sufferings of his passion and
death, just to be able to redeem ourselves.
303

lessons.title: Cities of refuge
lessons.subtitle: Sermon XXVII
lessons.summary: (Deuteronomy 19:1-10; Job 11:3-20) The prudent legislative provision of cities of refuge in the Mosaic law can be considered a parable of salvation in the O.T. It certainly responded to a governmental need of the time. The custom of the “blood avenger” had been established since patriarchal times, when justice was administered in the family. The closest relative of an injured or murdered person received praise or censure from his clan, depending on his zeal to avenge...
content:
(Deuteronomy 19:1-10;
Job 11:3-20)
The prudent legislative provision of cities
of refuge in the Mosaic law can be considered
as a parable of salvation in the O.T. It certainly responded to a governmental need of the time. The custom of the "avenger of the
"blood" had been established since the times
patriarchal, when justice was administered family-wise. The closest relative of an injured or murdered person received praise or censure from his
clan, according to their zeal in avenging the dead. It was not possible to suppress such a custom at once. However,
such a primitive method of justice lent itself to all
type of errors, since it did not give rise to verification
of the facts. The avenger acted on mere supposition or suspicion. In such circumstances, God had
to provide a circumstantial remedy: Six Levitical cities, spread throughout the country, would serve as
shelter; not to protect criminals, but to
give time to the action of justice, removing the
alleged murderer at the hands of the avenger.
304
The same biblical story presents us with a very good case.
possible. That of two lumberjacks who go out together
job, and one of them has the misfortune that his
ax slips from his hand or handle and goes
to fall unluckily on the head of his companion. The involuntary homicide has two paths:
Admit guilty and run to the city of Refugio, or ignore it, moving away from the
place, although this last resort would always be the
worse. There would be clues to his apparent crime, perhaps
Someone would have seen them go out into the field together.
The avenger rises in search of him. The murderer
becomes aware, runs in search of the path that leads to the
city of Refuge; The avenger pursues him. both
They run with all their strength. Panting the first,
Will he be able to arrive in time? Every time the
head, see the avenger closer; but you can already see the city in the distance. He makes a supreme effort to maintain a distance from his adversary, which is becoming shorter by the moment; but finally, exhausting his power to the maximum, he makes a superhuman effort and manages to cross the door, which the
sentry closes quickly behind him. The avenger,
furious, he throws the ax trying to hit him in the
last moment, but it remains stuck in the
thick door He's safe.
What lessons can we draw from the present
example?
305
1. We have all sinned through recklessness
There are people who are evil at heart, but the vast majority are not deliberately evil. The
Nature, the environment, the tempter, are the cause of our sin. But aren't we guilty? Yeah; if not deliberately, by recklessness,
out of weakness, to listen to the tempter. (See the
anecdote The Brahman and the missionary.) That is why we are
exposed to damnation, God has no obligation to admit souls stained by the
sin (Romans 3:10). If we have not committed material homicides, we are guilty of many
moral homicides. "He who hates his brother
"He is a murderer," exclaims John (1 John 3:15).
2. We must recognize ourselves as sinners
Before an omnipotent and omniscient judge like
God, it's the only way to take. Who will deceive you? The Pharisee thought he could dazzle God
with the exposition of its virtues; but the publican
made the best of it by humbly confessing his
guilt. (See the anecdote The galley slave and the prince.)
3. We must seek refuge
Recognize and regret the reckless act
it was enough. The avenger would arrive while the murderer
was involuntarily regretting, and most likely
ble in those times is that he did not abide by
reasons. Fortunately there was a remedy: run
to the city of Refuge. So it is with the sinner.
The refuge of the soul is Christ (Isaiah 32:2 and Matthew
11:28). Go by faith to the Lord; confess sin;
apply the work of Christ to our soul by invoking
his promises, is the best path to take. God hasput this Refuge in compassion for our ignorance (Acts 17:30). There is no recourse for
rebellious angels, but yes for men.
But the refuge is in vain if we do not go to it.
Note that it does not say that God, taking into account
our ignorance will overlook everything, but
"denounce all men in all places,
let them repent." Jesus himself on the cross recognized the involuntary part of his persecutors ("not
"They know what they're doing." God heard his request
divine Son, but it was necessary for those interested
ran to the shelter on the day of Pentecost (Acts
2:37-41).
4. Before the avenger arrives
It has been said that death is the messenger of God
to bring souls to their heavenly home. This is
true, of course, for Christians; but for the
unconverted, death is the messenger of the devil; the
avenger of sin, who pursues us at the pace of the
time, and it must reach us with complete certainty. It is
a great imprudence to wait for him outside of Christ; es307
especially when the resource of his salvation
is known.
Many are ready to say: The avenger is
far; I'm still young. However true this was,
We all know that the avenger can come after us
the corner, in the form of a heart attack, cancer,
accident, etc. If you are young, thank God because
you have a life to serve the Lord, and less likely to be late, as often happens
with those who begin to run, that is, to think about
God and his salvation, on the deathbed. (See
the anecdote The young man who missed the train.)
5. We must run on the true path
"There is a way that seems right to a man, but
Their end is the ways of death” (Proverbs 16:25).
It is not enough to run along any path, but you must
look for the real one. Many tire in vain
running down wrong paths (illustrate yourself with some
case of Indian fakirs or Mohammedan holy men).
Even in our nominally Christian countries,
There are many who run on lost paths,
relying on their own merits or resources
superstitious
Only in Christ is there complete satisfaction
for the soul that flees from sin.
308
6. We must remain in Christ
Once converted, the enemy is left outside
of the city of Refuge stalking the saved.
Peter compares him to a roaring lion. It is true that
Christ has promised to keep us and says: "My sheep
No one will snatch them out of my hand." But we can't
abuse such a statement. Christ also knew the
promise of Scripture to the “righteous man,” the Messiah: “He will command his angels to guard you,” yet He did not commit the imprudence of
throw himself from the battlements of the temple. By leaving the refuge we expose ourselves to the enemy
cause us to lose, if not the very salvation, then much of the
prize that God would like to give us; and we can still
remain completely indifferent. (See the anecdote Le
cost his soul.) Let us follow Christ closely, let us remain united to Him by faith and love. Then we
We will feel and be safe.
7. We must ensure that the posts on the road
    be clear to others
We need to remember that we are not the
only sinners for whom Christ died. Duty
Ours is to facilitate salvation for others. Isaiah 35:8 is
a precious promise for the Millennium; but, between
Therefore, the paths that lead to salvation can
be very poorly cared for. When people make mistakes,
misjudging the value of religion,
309
Isn't it often the fault of Christians themselves? As it was commanded to the Israelites in
As for the cities of refuge, we must
clearly indicate the path of salvation to sinners, with our words and with our example. The world is full of wandering sinners
They do not seek salvation, or they go down wrong paths. Let's live for them. Let's raise the flag of
salvation. Let's bring them to Christ.
ANECDOTES
THE BRAMAN AND THE MISSIONARY
A certain Brahman approached a missionary who waspreaching in the open air and raised the objection:
If the devil is the one who tempts us to sin, we do not
we are responsible. God had to punish the devil and not
to us.
The missionary answered:
–Do you see those men who are unloading
goods from a boat on the river bank? If I
I hand over a revolver and give him the bad advice to murder them
and steal their merchandise, who will the judges punish,
you or me?
“Both,” the objector answered without hesitation. A
you for having advised me and facilitated the crime, and
to me as a criminal.
–God will proceed in exactly the same way in his
fair trial. The sinners will be punished, but on the day
Blo and his agents, the demons, will not be spared
of his bad performance for centuries in this world.
THE GALEOTE AND THE PRINCE
A French prince, on the occasion of a visit that
made to the Marseille arsenal, decided to release one of
the criminals there condemned to row in the galleys.
In order to investigate who would be the most worthy of such
Merced interrogated several of the prisoners, who
They defended their guilt, alleging that other people who disliked them testified against them unfairly. Finally he reached a modest and humble condemned man,
who confessed his guilt without palliatives of any kind.
The prince, admired for his sincerity and humility,
Addressing the head of the fortress, he said ironically:
–We cannot allow so many good people to be
in contact with this very bad man. Let this be the one
receive the pardon.
TOO LATE
A certain young man arrived madly at the station in the
moment when the last car of the train passed in front of his eyes.
-What a pity! –he said with a scream that made the man turn
station chief. After having run with all my
forces…; I couldn't run anymore...
–I understand it, young man –said the boss–, but I
I'm afraid you started running a little too much.
afternoon.
311
IT COST HIM HIS SOUL
Two ministers of the Gospel were walking through the outskirts of a certain town, and they arrived at a beautiful farm.
where there was a magnificent house surrounded by a good
well-kept orchard that belonged to a former member of
the church.
–How much would this property cost its owner? –the visitor asked the local pastor.
"I don't know, in terms of money," answered the person questioned, "but I'm very afraid that it has cost him his soul."
In other times the owner of this land was a
enthusiastic member of the church, attending all
cults; but since he began to get rich, and after
of acquiring this property, you have been so absorbed in your
Be careful, we haven't seen him anymore in the church, and
seems to have become totally indifferent to the
things of God. Although he said that he had acquired it from
bargain price, I'm afraid you paid a price for it
too high: that of his own soul.
312

lessons.title: Heavenly identity card
lessons.subtitle: Sermon XXVIII
lessons.summary: HEAVENLY IDENTITY CARD (Revelation 2:17) Appealing to the customs of his people and his time, Our Lord Jesus Christ used curious figures when addressing men and expressing his purpose of salvation. During his earthly ministry we see him present the figures of the yoke, the water, the bread, the sower, the prodigal son, etc. Before entering the era of grace, which is also that of the testing of faith, in his revelation to the apostle John, on Patmos, he also uses, in a more brief way,…
content:
CARD
OF CELESTIAL IDENTITY
(Revelation 2:17)
Appealing to the customs of his people and his
era, Our Lord Jesus Christ used curious figures
when addressing men and expressing his purpose
of salvation.
During his earthly ministry we see him present the figures of the yoke, the water, the bread, the sower, the prodigal son, etc. Before entering the
era of grace, which is also that of the test of
faith, in its revelation to the apostle John, on Patmos, uses
also, in a more brief way, curious figures: the
of the alphabet (1:8), that of the temple (3:12), of the door
(3:20), etc. Without a doubt, the most curious of all is that of
the little white stone (2:17) that many will have read
more than once wondering: What does it mean? Why
What does the Lord use such a strange example?
1. The “tessera hospitalis”
We are told that the Romans had a curious
custom. When two people entered into a
313
deep friendship, one staying at home
of the other, if the host wanted when saying goodbye to his
hosted to seal their friendship in a perennial way,
He took a small square marble tablet, on which
He made an incision with a steel burin, and with the
He himself wrote on one side the name of the person staying and on the other his own. Immediately, the stone was broken with a sharp blow.
and half of the stone that contained the name of the
host was delivered to the host, and the part
which contained the name of the former, remained in the possession of the latter.
If after many years one of the two wanted
resume the friendship, if he needed any favors from
another, taking the little marble stone that contained
his friend's name was addressed to his friend's home;
and if this one survived, but the years had changed their mutual appearances, the little stone
white served as a piece of identification to make him
remember his promises; or if he had died
the giver, the relatives had the duty to respect the
sign of friendship that the tessera hospitalis meant.
A servant was looking for the other half in the stone archive
of the house, and if the matching part was found,
could count on the benevolence of the old friend or
of his relatives.
We live in other times, and we have
other more practical means of identification, but
"Jesus Christ is the same, yesterday, today and forever,"
and what he explained to the people of his century with figures
314
and practical examples of his time, he also told us
to us.
Let us observe, then, the main teachings
of this curious example.
2. The conditions of the recipient
The little white stone was not given to just anyone,
but to the person who was entitled to this privilege and with whom they wanted to establish an intimate relationship.
friendship. In the spiritual case, the Lord says: "To him who
If he wins, I will give him a little white stone.
Many times the Gospel is presented to us
as a free gift from God, free, of pure grace,
and others, perhaps, immediately afterwards, they talk about it
as a reward or result of great effort.
For example, in 21:6 and 7 of Revelation.
How to combine the statements of both texts?
We have an illustration in the case of David and
the well of Bethlehem in 11:16-19 of 1st Chronicles. The water
It was certainly free, it flowed generously
inside the well and was within reach of anyone,
but the difficult thing, in that case, was getting there.
It was necessary to be brave, a hero in such
circumstances. Many times, through the centuries,
The saying of the Lord has been fulfilled: "In the Kingdom of
the heavens become strong, and the mighty take it away. In our nation our ancestors
They needed to be brave to approach the
source. (See Spanish Harvest, a new book by
315
the origins of evangelical work in Galicia,
Spain).
Even in politically free countries, it is difficult today to be a Christian, especially to live as a Christian... We have to fight every day with well-intentioned friends who try to distract us and separate us from the
narrow path, or with one's own heart, the selfcomplacent and selfish of each one. There are thousands of
small and big victories to be won. But they are certainly worth earning. Observe the privileges of the significant figure.
3. The new name of the Giver
In chapter 19:13 of this mystery book of "The
Revelation", Jesus appears to John with his name
old; the one that Philo sensed and John emphasizes in the
first chapter of his gospel, "The Word of God."
That is, the visible manifestation of divinity
invisible (John 1:18).
There is a mysterious biblical phrase in Micah 5:2
that opens up an unfathomable horizon for us regarding this
name and person of Christ before his incarnation. After announcing his birth in Bethlehem
of Judea, says the prophet: "Whose going out is from the
eternity, from the days of the ages" (the days of the
Olam, according to the Hebrew original). What do they mean
such "departures" of the child who was to be born in Bethlehem?
The traditional theological interpretation of this
passage was applying it to theophanies or revelations
316
from the Almighty to Adam, Abraham, Jacob, Moses,
etc.; but the language seems disproportionate to me
of Micah to refer only to these three or
four biblical cases. Why not think about a unfolding, perhaps multiple, of the Divine Word in a
be visible, to reveal itself (like Theophany, naturally) to other races of the Universe represented in
the sayings of Jesus for the ninety-nine righteous
that they do not need repentance? In such "outings"
He acted as the Word of God, revealer of the invisible Being (John 1:18). But the departure of the divine Word to this
tiny, but beautiful “blue planet” of the system
solar, which the angels celebrated on the night of
Christmas is a totally different manifestation.
Not a theophany, but an incarnation, a real and
positive identification of the Word with a fallen race
to restore it, to redeem it, to save it from
ruin of sin and elevate it to very high destinies, and
This gives rise to a new name for the divine
Verb. Which? The glorious name of Savior
(Philippians 2:9).
This new, honorable, and glorious name of
our Redeemer, must be engraved on the
little white stone that represents us, that is, about
our heart. Is it? Can we say, like the
blessed virgin, "My spirit rejoiced in God my
“Savior”?
And our name must be up there, in
the other part of the emblematic "little white stone."
317
"Rejoice that your names are written in
the Book of Life," said Jesus.
Is our name there?
4. The secret of the new name
«A new name... that no one can understand but
"he who possesses it," our text continues to say.
The name engraved with the stiletto on the tessera
hospitalis meant nothing, it said nothing to a stranger, but to its owner it meant pleasant memories
and flattering hopes of favors enjoyed and
promised.
That's how it is with Christians. "The world does not know us because it does not know Him." For Juan, the name
Jesus meant everything, he was an apostle of the Lord
with a most glorious eternal future. To the soldier, or soldiers, who guarded him on Patmos, John
He was a poor old man who had fallen into the displeasure of
the Roman authorities; but he knew the promises of Christ and could express them with the eloquent
language of 1st John 3:1-3.
This is the wonderful security of every Christian. (See the anecdote The colporteur Félix Vacas and the
General Aguilera.)
5. The adaptation of the two parts
The little white stone, which is a figure of ourselves, adapted to its other half, because it was
318
broken, not sawn. And we adapt to
Lord Jesus? Do we have a moral identity with Him
that makes us fit for heaven, that is, to live in his glorious company, and that of holy angels
for eternal centuries? Have we adapted to your
character? Do we look like Him? (See anecdote
He lives near my house.) Is ourcharacter to that of Christ that we could thus be confused with Him? Everyone wants to go to heaven, but
few make the effort to adapt for heaven. Fortunately, the Gospel we preach has
this undeniable transformative power, still recognized
by his enemies. (The savages of the Land of Fire
and other examples from the Encyclopedia of Anecdotes, pp.
183-194, section VIII; Christian Life: Transformation
for the conversion. ) Christian discipleship is a
adaptation of our character to that of Him to whom
we owe everything (2 Corinthians 3:18). Also this
requires a fight.
6. The privileges of the heavenly secret
God always has high and unfathomable motives
for all his actions, because his infinite mind encompasses
the past, the present and the future. Who would have
said, when he began to create the raw material of the
world what on this tiny but beautiful planet had
what to develop? And who can say, when
God calls a Christian, perhaps a simple and humble spiritual stone of his church, the purposes
319
What does it have for that individual being in the unfathomable centuries of eternity? The parables of the minas and the talents give us some glimpse of
this, but we all understand that it will be something more
great and glorious than what we can from here
imagine Will we be prepared to occupy the
place that you have prepared for us?
Apart from such parables, there are phrases of the Savior that give us a lot to think about, such as
Luke 16:10, 11: "The little," in this significant passage, is what is despicable, what is fleeting; "how much" is what
definitive, the eternal. However, this is the time
the test, to convert "the little" "into much", since
that we will never again go through circumstances of
life similar to the present ones. (See anecdote
Things we won't be able to do in heaven. )
For this reason we are admonished by the Lord himself, referring to the time of his second coming,
with the words: "Pray, watching at all times,
so that you may be counted worthy to avoid things
who are to come and stand before the Son of the
Man” (Luke 21:36). This means that we can
tell him like Peter: «Lord, you know all things»…, you know that I loved you, that I did not deny your name;
Despite all my weaknesses and infirmities, you
You know I've had a sincere heart for you. Do
from me whatever you want and how you want to serve you
Now, how I tried to do it, despite everything and
against everything, in my time of trial on earth.
Amen.
320
ANECDOTES
THE COLPORTOR FÉLIX COWS
AND GENERAL AGUILERA
In the time of King Alfonso XIII of Spain it was made
popular in the African wars the name of the general
Aguilera.
One day, a short, cross-eyed, and humbly man
dressed, he was at the door of a barracks in Ciudad
Real trying to sell copies of the Holy Scripture to the soldiers who were resting, sunbathing, during the guard period. It was the well-known colporteur Félix Vacas, the man who carried in his body
the marks of Christ, for some beatings he had received from fanatic enemies of Christianity
evangelical Suddenly, the brave canvasser found himself without
audience for having given the voice "to form." Moments later a gentleman got out of a luxurious car.
dressed in civilian clothes, who, watching the canvasser collect
hurriedly grabbed his merchandise, approached him to question him.
The humble servant of God continued his work, murmuring some excuse; due to the sergeant's fear and, above all,
everything, from the guard officer who, firm at his posts
They suspected they were trapped in some compromise, depending on the nature of the books. As the canvasser
He would hurry to finish his task with his head bowed,
The knight shouted to him:
–Look me in the face, man, and stand firm! Do you know
Who are you talking to?
321
"No, sir," answered the aforementioned.
–With General Aguilera.
–Excuse me, general, I had not recognized you.
dressed like that in civilian clothes.
Suddenly, one of those ideas came to the canvasser.sparkling, typical of its Andalusian character and its firm
Christian faith. Raising the head and stretching on the
tiptoe, exclaimed:
–And you, my general, do you know who you are talking to?
The officers' eyes sparkled with anger and those of
the troop of hilarious curiosity, when they heard the poor
peddler say:
–With the son of a King, sir general, with a son of
God. See how he says it here – and quickly opening a
N.T. showed him John 1:12, beginning an evangelizing talk that the general listened to benevolently by some
moments, and smiling he entered the barracks.
LIVE NEAR MY HOUSE
A certain Chinese girl entered a Sunday school room while the teacher was describing the person of the Lord Jesus Christ, praising his virtues, his
kindness, his love for children, the helpless and the
sick While the teacher was talking she saw the
girl who, with her little finger raised, showed, restlessly, desires
to speak The instructor interrupted her lecture and
Addressing the newcomer, he invited her to speak. Ante
To everyone's astonishment, the girl said:
–This man you are talking about, I know him.
He lives near my house.
322
Many children could not contain their laughter, knowing that the teacher was talking to them about the Lord Jesus who
is in Heaven. But the girl, undeterred, continued
referring to what she had seen from a missionary who
He lived a short distance from his house.
QUEEN VICTORIA'S OFFICER
In relation to the previous message, I remember the incident of an officer who said to Queen Victoria, in a
reception which took place in the royal palace of His Britannic Majesty, who was anxious to have him declared
some war in which he could show his love and
loyalty to his sovereignty and country. When reading this anecdote
I have wondered if someday in eternity, taken
for our loyalty and growing admiration for our
adored Redeemer, we will not say to ourselves: "Who could live
again in a world of sinners to be able to do,
for the love of our King, difficult things, heroic things and
self-sacrificing, which we neglect today!
THINGS WE CANNOT DO IN HEAVEN
It impressed me when I was young, and I have referred to it
succinctly many times by way of illustration, a sermon I heard in Nîmes from the blind preacher Mr. Jalaguier,
on this topic.
The preacher mentioned three things that we will not be able to
do in heaven:
1. Preach salvation to lost sinners, well not
there will be them in that blessed place.
323
2. Give of what is ours to God, because we will live in holiness
heavenly community where there will be neither yours nor mine.
3. He emphasized the third thing as the easiest, the most
at hand for everyone, but the most difficult. Something that everyone
we can do here, but there will be no chance
some to practice there: loving and forgiving our
offenders, because we will all be perfect there.
These three things we must strive to do
here, since we will never have the opportunity to put them into practice again. It is here where we have the opportunity to
show the Lord the value and effectiveness of our faith, in
circumstances that will not occur again in centuries
of eternity.
324

lessons.title: The parable of the plow
lessons.subtitle: Sermon XXIX
lessons.summary: THE PARABLE OF THE PLOW (Luke 10:17-24; Matthew 11:25-30) 1. The reason for the great invitation Jesus' well-known phrase, "Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest," has a beautiful setting. In other words, in favor of the will of God

I was excited, at the father's will. We can never

JOSEPH, FIGURE OF CHRIST
(Psalm 105:1-23)
The story of Joseph is, without a doubt, the most comprehensive and admirable historical narrative in the O.T. The
Holy Spirit brought events for good
of Joseph and his people, but he himself was able to do
so that he was a type of the future Messiah. It is
This similarity is admirable, knowing that it occurred almost
2,000 years ago. This can be considered a
proof of both the inspiration of the Bible and
the divinity of Christ.
Let us observe fourteen similarities between this historical figure of the patriarchal age and our Lord
Jesus Christ.
1. Beloved of his Father
See Genesis 37:3-8. So does Christ. God
He has millions of millions of children by creation,

It is the Word (Colossians 1:15). Angels are pure

342

so that they would torment him less, but he preferred

Joseph, for the jailer; Christ, through Pilate and the
centurion
345

(Isaiah 53:8). Certainly, an existence like that of
human beings, with the inevitable end of death,
It must have seemed like an imprisonment to the celestials, who saw Christ, the Divine Word, in such a condition.
10. They were both extraordinary
